title: Digital leadership and supply chain maturity: The role of digital transformation in sustainable performance
summary: Purpose: Responding to the growing needs of the global markets to be sustainable amid the rapid digitalization of the economy, the proposed study aims at exploring the degree to which Digital Leadership and Supply Chain Digital Maturity can collectively contribute to the Sustainable Supply Chain Performance and Digital Transformation Practices serves as a intervening factor between the two variables.Design/methodology/approach: Using the Dynamic Capabilities Theory (DCT) as a tool of analysis, the study follows the quantitative, cross-sectional methodology, gathering information among professionals (384) carrying out their functions in supply-chain and digital-transformation fields. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) is used through Smart-PLS 4.0 in order to test the relationship as postulated in the construct.Findings: The findings show that Digital Leadership and Supply Chain Digital Maturity have a significant effect on Sustainable Supply Chain Performance, whereas Digital Transformation Practices are the mediating variable without which the connection between the two variables is not possible.Research limitations/implications: Such ?ndings underline the necessity to align digital capabilities played at the internal level and strategic transformation efforts in order to achieve sustainability goals.Practical implications: As a theoretical contribution, the study transfers DCT to the digital supply-chain setting and provides managers a feasible framework in a quest to use digitalization to gain sustainable competitive advantage.Social implications: The study highlights the role of aligning digital capabilities and transformation efforts in achieving sustainability goals, which can contribute to broader economic and environmental benefits in global markets.Originality/value: As a theoretical contribution, the study transfers DCT to the digital supply-chain setting and provides managers a feasible framework in a quest to use digitalization to gain sustainable competitive advantage.

title: Linking digital transformation strategy, digital circular supply chains and sustainable supply chain performance: the moderating role of environmental dynamism
summary: Purpose This study investigates how digital transformation strategy (DTS) influences sustainable supply chain performance (SSCP) through digital circular supply chains (DCSC) in manufacturing SMEs in an emerging market economy such as Vietnam. It also investigates whether environmental dynamism (ED) moderates the relationships between DTS and DCSC, and between DCSC and SSCP. Design/methodology/approach Primary data were captured using a tailored questionnaire, a quantitative methodology was employed. The model incorporated moderated mediation and tested using survey data from 468 managers/directors in Vietnam’s manufacturing SME. It employs partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) technique to evaluate the proposed hypotheses. Findings The results show that DTS positively affects SSCP both directly and indirectly. DCSC has a significant positive impact on SSCP and partially mediates the relationship between DTS and SSCP. Furthermore, ED moderated the relationships between DTS and DCSC as well as between DCSC and SSCP. Originality/value This study yields novel insights into how DTS drives SSCP through DCSC in manufacturing SMEs operating in emerging economies. It extends the literature by identifying ED as a critical boundary condition shaping the effectiveness of digital transformation. The findings yield valuable implications for managers seeking to leverage digital strategies and circular technologies to enhance SSCP.

title: Governing for sustainability in a dynamic environment: the roles of corporate governance, organizational capabilities and entrepreneurial culture in Indonesian rural banks
summary: This study examines the determinants of sustainable performance among Indonesian Rural Banks (BPRs) by integrating Information Technology Adoption (IT), Internal Control (IC), Human Capital Capability (HC), and Good Corporate Governance (GCG), while examining Environmental Dynamism (ED) as a moderating condition. Using a quantitative approach, the study employed Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with data from 436 BPR respondents and a second-order construct specification. The findings show that Internal Control and Human Capital Capability have significant positive effects on BPR Sustainable Performance, whereas Information Technology Adoption has no significant direct effect. Information Technology Adoption and Internal Control significantly influence GCG, while Human Capital Capability does not. GCG has a significant positive effect on Sustainable Performance and selectively mediates the effects of Information Technology Adoption and Internal Control, but not Human Capital Capability. Environmental Dynamism positively moderates the relationship between GCG and Sustainable Performance. The study contributes to the sustainable performance literature by integrating technological, organizational, governance, and environmental perspectives within a unified second-order PLS-SEM framework. The findings demonstrate that technology adoption alone does not guarantee sustainable performance; its contribution is more effectively realized when supported by effective governance and organizational control mechanisms.

title: Tail-Dependent Connectedness Across Carbon, Water, Clean-Energy, Green-Bond, and ESG Markets
summary: Sustainable financial markets link carbon pricing, environmental infrastructure, low-carbon technology, fixed-income financing, and broad environmental, social, and governance investment. Whether these markets transmit shocks differently in the tails of the return distribution remains important for diversification and transition-risk management. This study examines return connectedness among European Union Allowance prices, a global water exchange-traded fund, a global clean-energy index, a U.S.-dollar green-bond exchange-traded fund, and an ESG equity index. The synchronized sample contains 1441 daily level observations from 16 March 2020 to 31 December 2025, yielding 1440 percentage log returns. A quantile vector autoregression is combined with generalized forecast-error variance decomposition to estimate total, directional, and net connectedness at the 0.05, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, and 0.95 quantiles. Rolling estimates, stationary-bootstrap confidence intervals, volatility and interest-rate regimes, and forecast-horizon sensitivity provide additional inference. Full-sample total connectedness is moderate and unusually stable, ranging from 33.90% to 34.16%. Rolling evidence nevertheless reveals statistically supported upper-tail amplification: the 0.95-quantile total connectedness exceeds the median by 0.672 percentage points on average, with a 95% stationary-bootstrap interval of 0.372 to 0.961. The lower-tail difference is not statistically distinguishable from zero. The water–equity portfolio is the most persistent net transmitter, while green bonds are the principal net receiver. High-VIX windows exhibit lower rather than higher average connectedness. An exact cluster decomposition attributes this decline to weaker cross-cluster links, while connectedness within the CGW–CLEAN–SPESG equity cluster rises slightly. Extreme conditional returns and observable market stress are therefore related but distinct states. The findings support state-contingent diversification and caution against assuming that all forms of stress mechanically intensify integration among sustainable assets. A strictly timed out-of-sample extension shows that a state-contingent QVAR-adjusted minimum-variance portfolio reduces annualized volatility from 13.22% for equal weighting to 5.91% and maximum drawdown from 21.39% to 13.22%, although this protection is accompanied by lower realized returns. Connectedness therefore provides decision value primarily through risk containment rather than return enhancement in this sample. Window-length sensitivity qualifies the rolling asymmetry: upper-tail differences remain positive at 400 and 600 observations, but the 600-observation stationary-bootstrap interval includes zero; lower-tail contrasts become significant under both alternative windows. The main tail inference is therefore conditional on rolling-window choice.

title: Practice of Digital Transformation of Intelligent Education Management in Higher Vocational Colleges
summary: Wisdom drives the transformation of higher vocational governance, but process fragmentation, data islands, and lagging performance hinder the change. This study relies on 850,000 multi-source logs from two provincial higher vocational colleges from 2019 to 2024 to build a “business-data” dual-loop model. The authors optimize the closed-loop of approval and strengthen real-time quality inspection and analysis. Empirical evidence shows that the longer the approval chain, the more frequent the rework. Experiments show that the approval time is reduced, and the satisfaction is increased. The authors innovatively design a three-layer five-dimensional indicator system and a dual-loop state machine and embed interpretable AI feedback to form a generalizable precise governance paradigm.

title: The Heterogeneous Impacts of Digital Transformation on Firms’ Internationalization: Evidence from China
summary: Using Chinese A-share-listed firms from 2013 to 2023, this study examines whether and how digital transformation affects firm internationalization. We measure internationalization along both the intensive and extensive margins, including overseas revenue share, overseas operating revenue, internationalization participation, and a BERT-based internationalization indicator constructed from annual reports. Digital transformation is mainly measured by firms’ digital intangible assets, and we further use digital patents, digital job postings, and annual-report digital keyword disclosure as alternative measures. The results show that digital transformation significantly promotes firm internationalization. A one-unit increase in the digital transformation is associated with a 1.3-percentage-point higher probability of internationalization and a 0.8-percentage-point higher overseas revenue share. Further analysis based on the Awareness-Motivation-Capability (AMC) framework shows that digital transformation promotes internationalization by improving firms’ awareness of overseas opportunities, strengthening their motivation to expand abroad, and enhancing their capabilities through higher productivity and lower financing constraints. The effect is more pronounced among firms with higher initial productivity, suggesting that preexisting capabilities affect how firms convert digital investment into international expansion. Evidence from recruitment data further shows that digital transformation is associated with higher demand for highly educated workers, indicating that human-capital upgrading is an important part of this process. Overall, this study provides firm-level evidence that digital transformation supports Chinese firms’ internationalization by improving both market expansion and organizational capabilities.

title: Evidence-oriented managerial decision-making for digital transformation of business processes in agricultural enterprises
summary: Purpose. This paper addresses a practical problem that often appears after a digital project is introduced: managers can see that a technology is in use, but they may still lack enough evidence to explain what changed in the business process and whether the observed result can be attributed to that change. The aim is to develop an evidence-oriented decision mechanism for digital transformation in agricultural enterprises. Design/methodology/approach. The approach follows the chain from a documented digital intervention to a change in the managerial mechanism and then to a process-related outcome. It also considers regulatory and sustainability constraints, persistence of the result, and the strength of the available evidence. The logic is examined using documented cases of Ukrainian agricultural enterprises and open operational, financial, and contextual information. Findings. The analysis identifies six recurring situations: cautious scaling with stronger measurement, collecting missing evidence before an investment claim, changing an unsuitable KPI, using a strong enterprise as a benchmark without digital attribution, separating digital and non-digital changes, and using non-digital interventions as comparison cases. Five evidence levels distinguish descriptive evidence from stronger causal claims. Research limitations/implications. The open data are heterogeneous and do not support a common counterfactual design. Practical implications. The mechanism helps managers decide what can be acted on now and what must be measured first. Originality/value. The study links process evidence directly to the strength of the managerial decision rather than to an aggregate digital score. JEL Classification: M10, M11, O33, Q12.

title: Developing future managers’ skills in using CRM systems as a factor in the development of human capital mobility in the digital economy
summary: У статті досліджено формування умінь майбутніх менеджерів використовувати CRM-системи як чинник розвитку мобільності людського капіталу в умовах цифрової економіки. Актуальність дослідження зумовлена цифровою трансформацією бізнесу, поширенням штучного інтелекту, аналітики великих даних та автоматизації бізнес-процесів, що формують нові вимоги до професійних компетентностей управлінців. Метою статті є теоретичне обґрунтування та розроблення концептуальної економічної моделі формування CRM-компетентностей майбутніх менеджерів і визначення механізмів їх впливу на цифровий людський капітал, мобільність людського капіталу, продуктивність праці та конкурентоспроможність підприємства. Методологічну основу становлять системний, компетентнісний, ресурсний і процесний підходи, положення теорії людського капіталу, ресурсної теорії підприємства та теорії динамічних здібностей. Запропоновано авторську модель послідовного створення економічної цінності: «CRM-компетентності → цифровий людський капітал → мобільність людського капіталу → продуктивність праці → конкурентоспроможність підприємства». Визначено латентні конструкції та їх індикатори й обґрунтовано можливість емпіричної перевірки моделі методом PLS-SEM. Розкрито медіаційний механізм трансформації CRM-компетентностей у конкурентні результати через розвиток цифрового людського капіталу, професійної мобільності та продуктивності праці. Наукова новизна полягає в інтеграції компетентнісного підходу, теорії людського капіталу та цифрового менеджменту в єдину концептуальну модель розвитку конкурентних переваг підприємства. Практичне значення полягає у можливості використання моделі для вдосконалення освітніх програм підготовки менеджерів, корпоративного навчання, оцінювання цифрових компетентностей персоналу та формування політики розвитку людського капіталу. Обмеженням дослідження є концептуальний характер моделі, що потребує подальшої емпіричної перевірки. JEL класифікація: M15, M53, J24, O33.

title: The Impact of Supply Chain Finance on Green Innovation in Listed Firms: A Supply-Demand Mismatch Perspective
summary: Under China's carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals, supply chain finance (SCF) is widely regarded as a practical way to ease the financing constraints on green innovation in listed firms. Its enabling effect, however, remains limited. Drawing on the literature on SCF and green innovation, this paper argues that the constraint is not simply a shortage of credit but a structural mismatch between the supply of and demand for funds. First, the short maturity of most SCF products does not fit the multi-year horizon of green R&D. Second, credit assessment centered on tangible trade assets struggles to recognize the value of green patents, process know-how, and other intangible outputs. Third, weak incentive alignment and fragmented coordination across organizational units reduce the likelihood that additional liquidity reaches green R&D. Accordingly, the paper proposes longer-dated and milestone-based SCF products, a revised credit assessment framework that incorporates green intangible assets, and stronger incentive and coordination mechanisms. The central implication is that SCF can support green innovation only when product design, organizational routines, and external institutions are aligned with the distinctive funding needs of green projects.

title: Green Accounting and Intellectual Capital Efficiency as Drivers of Firm Value: Evidence from the Indonesian Mining Sector
summary: Post-pandemic economic conditions have increased the relevance of environmental performance and intangible resources in investor assessments, particularly in environmentally intensive industries. This study examines the relationship between PROPER-based environmental performance, intellectual capital efficiency, and firm value among mining companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) from 2021 to 2024. Using purposive sampling, the study analyzes 40 observations from 10 companies through panel data regression with the REM in Stata 15. The results indicate that environmental performance is negatively associated with firm value in both models, with and without control variables (b = −0.24, p = 0.048; b = −0.31, p = 0.021, respectively). Human capital efficiency is positively associated with firm value in the model with control variables (b = 0.019, p = 0.017). Structural capital efficiency and relational capital efficiency are not statistically significant in either model, while capital employed efficiency is significant only in the model without control variables. Higher PROPER ratings do not guarantee higher market valuations, while human capital efficiency may better attract investors. Companies should communicate environmental performance and develop employee capabilities, while regulators should ensure transparent and consistent environmental reporting.

title: ANALYSIS OF THE IMPLEMENTATION OF BLUE ACCOUNTING IN SUPPORTING ACCOUNTABILITY OF MARINE RESOURCE MANAGEMENT IN WEST KALIMANTAN
summary: This study aims to analyze the implementation of blue accounting in supporting accountability for marine resource management at the Marine and Fisheries Agency of West Kalimantan Province. The study employs a qualitative method with a descriptive approach and a case study design. Data were collected through in-depth interviews with three informants, observation, and documentation. Informants were selected based on their direct involvement in financial management and the management of marine and coastal ecosystems. Data were analyzed using thematic analysis and triangulated based on the findings from interviews, observation, and documentation. The results indicate that the implementation of blue accounting is still in its early stages and has not yet been fully integrated into financial management and marine resource reporting. The accounting system used adheres to accrual-based Government Accounting Standards (SAP) but does not yet incorporate the economic and ecological values ​​of marine resources into financial reporting. Key challenges include limited data availability, insufficient human resource capacity, the absence of specific policies and regulatory frameworks, limited information system integration, and budgetary constraints. Costs associated with environmental protection and restoration are still recorded under general operational activities. Despite these limitations, blue accounting has the potential to strengthen transparency and accountability by integrating financial, economic, and ecological information into marine resource management.

title: Fintech Regulation and Corporate Digital Transformation: Evidence from the Regulatory Sandbox Pilot in China
summary: Against the backdrop of rapidly evolving Fintech and its accelerating integration with traditional finance, how financial regulation shapes corporate innovation has emerged as an important issue. Yet the mechanisms through which Fintech regulation promotes or inhibits corporate digital transformation remain underexplored. Drawing on a sample of Chinese A-share listed firms from 2015 to 2022 and exploiting the "Regulatory Sandbox" pilot as a quasi-natural experiment, this paper examines the effect of Fintech regulation on corporate digital transformation. The results show that Fintech regulation significantly promotes corporate digital transformation, supporting the signaling effect hypothesis. This conclusion remains robust to alternative measures of the dependent variable, parallel trend tests, PSM-DID, and placebo tests. Further analyses reveal that: (1) the promoting effect is more pronounced among firms with lower fixed-asset intensity, lower audit quality, and lower analyst coverage; (2) Fintech regulation facilitates digital transformation by alleviating firms' financing constraints. This study not only provides evidence that regulatory policy influences corporate digital transformation through the financing-environment channel, but also demonstrates that effective Fintech regulation establishes an institutional foundation conducive to digital transformation.

title: Fintechs et intégration socio-économique : le cas des immigrés subsahariens au Maroc
summary: Résumé L’inclusion financière des immigrés subsahariens au Maroc constitue un levier important de leur intégration socio-économique. Dans un contexte de développement des innovations financières (paiements mobiles, fintechs et microfinance digitale), cette étude analyse leur contribution à l’amélioration de l’accès et de l’utilisation des services financiers. Elle vise également à identifier les obstacles qui limitent leur portée et les conditions nécessaires à une inclusion durable. En mobilisant une méthodologie mixte, fondée sur un questionnaire administré à 100 immigrés subsahariens et sur 25 entretiens semi-directifs menés auprès de 15 immigrés, de 5 responsables d’institutions financières et de 5 responsables d’associations, les résultats mettent en évidence un double constat. D’une part, les services financiers numériques favorisent l’autonomie économique et contribuent à l’amélioration de la qualité de vie, notamment à travers les paiements mobiles et les transferts de fonds. D’autre part, des obstacles structurels persistent, en particulier les contraintes administratives, les barrières linguistiques et la méfiance envers les institutions financières. L’effet favorable des innovations financières apparaît ainsi conditionné par le contexte institutionnel et les caractéristiques des utilisateurs. La pérennité de leurs effets suppose un accompagnement ciblé, des mesures institutionnelles adaptées - notamment en matière de procédures d’identification des clients (KYC), de régulation des fintechs et de protection des consommateurs - ainsi que des partenariats entre banques, fintechs et associations, afin de favoriser une inclusion financière plus durable et équitable. Mots clés : Inclusion Financière ; Innovations Financières ; Immigrés Subsahariens ; Maroc ; Fintechs ; Paiements Mobiles ; Intégration Socio-Economique. Abstract Financial inclusion among Sub-Saharan immigrants in Morocco is an important lever for socio-economic integration. Against the backdrop of expanding financial innovations, including mobile payments, fintechs, and digital microfinance, this study examines their contribution to improving access to and use of financial services. It also identifies the barriers limiting their effectiveness and the conditions required for sustainable inclusion. The study adopts a mixed-methods approach based on a survey of 100 Sub-Saharan immigrants and 25 semi-structured interviews with 15 immigrants, 5 representatives of financial institutions, and 5 representatives of NGOs and associations. The findings reveal a twofold outcome. On the one hand, digital financial services support economic autonomy and contribute to improved quality of life, particularly through mobile payments and remittances. On the other hand, structural barriers persist, including administrative requirements, language barriers, and distrust of financial institutions. The beneficial effects of financial innovations therefore appear to depend on institutional conditions and users’ characteristics. Their sustainability requires targeted support, appropriate institutional measures - including suitable know-your-customer (KYC) procedures, fintech regulation, and consumer protection - and partnerships between banks, fintechs, and associations to promote more sustainable and equitable financial inclusion. title: From digital maturity to managerial performance: a methodology for evaluating digital transformation in private healthcare organizations
summary: Purpose. This article develops an integrated methodology that connects digital maturity with implementation quality, process change, managerial performance, and strategic value in private healthcare organizations. Design/methodology/approach. A structured integrative review and framework synthesis combined 27 substantive sources from digital-maturity research, implementation science, information-systems evaluation, health economics, and authoritative digital-health guidance; two additional publications informed the review method. Findings. The resulting Maturity-to-Performance Evaluation Framework (M2P-EF) distinguishes six evaluation layers: investment and digital assets, maturity capabilities, implementation quality, process and behavioral change, managerial performance, and strategic value. The layers are assessed across seven domains: strategic governance; data, infrastructure, interoperability, and cybersecurity; process integration and productivity; workforce capability; patient value, quality, access, and equity; financial and market sustainability; and resilience. The methodology also specifies indicator rules, noncompensatory safety and governance gates, an evidence ladder, economic analysis, and a seven-step decision protocol. Practical implications. M2P-EF can guide prospective evaluation, help managers distinguish implementation failure from value-proposition failure, and support transparent decisions to continue, modify, scale, pause, or discontinue digital initiatives. Research limitations/implications. The framework has not yet been empirically validated; content validation, feasibility testing, psychometric assessment, and longitudinal multisite evaluation are required before comparative use. Originality/value. The main contribution is to define digital maturity as an enabling capability rather than an organizational outcome and to measure it separately from performance. title: The Influence of Institutional Ownership, Managerial Ownership, Independent Board of Commissioners, Audit Comittee on Company Values (Study of Banking Companies Listed On The IDX For The 2020-2023 Period)
summary: Abstract: Good Corporate Governance (GCG) plays a crucial role in determining a company's value, with factors such as institutional and managerial ownership, the independent board of commissioners, and the audit committee significantly influencing investor decisions. In the banking sector, fluctuations in income, asset ratios, and equity ratios can impact investor confidence and decision-making. This study aims to examine the influence of institutional ownership, managerial ownership, the independent board of commissioners, and the audit committee on company value. Using a quantitative associative approach, the research analyzes a sample of 88 companies selected through purposive sampling, a non-probability sampling method. Data were collected from the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) and official company websites, and analyzed using SPSS Version 26. The results of the findings showed that: (H1) accepted; (H2) rejected; (H3) rejected; (H4) accepted; (H5) accepted. The results imply that governance mechanisms should be considered separately, as audit committee effectiveness and institutional ownership, and non-significant associations need not be interpreted as uniform governance effects.

title: Technology-Governance Coordination Mechanisms in the Digitalization of ESG Information Disclosure: A Multi-case Comparative Study of Microsoft, Siemens, and Tesla
summary: Under the background of an persistently increasing ESG regulatory requirements, the enterprise ESG still faces problems of information disclosure such as data fragmentation, standard adaptation challenges, and information credibility deficits. However, the extent to which digital technology improves ESG disclosure quality is determined by technological application capabilities and enterprise governance effectiveness. To explore how technical capabilities and governance conditions interact to shape ESG information disclosure, this paper conducts a multi-case comparative analysis of three multinational firms, including Microsoft, Siemens, and Tesla, based on information asymmetry theory, signaling theory, and agency theory, to examine the effects of digital technology applications and governance mechanisms on ESG disclosure quality. The study shows that digital technology improves ESG disclosure quality via the support of effective governance conditions. The integration of technology application with data management, organizational mechanisms, and external supervision boosts the transparency and verifiability of ESG information, while inadequate governance mechanisms limit the contribution of technological applications to disclosure quality improvement.

title: Research on FinTech Reshaping Enterprise Investment and Financing Modes from the Corporate Finance Perspective
summary: The traditional financial system has long suffered from structural drawbacks. Issues such as an imperfect information disclosure mechanism and a simplistic risk pricing model have persisted for a long time, thereby artificially raising the transaction costs in the investment and financing processes of real enterprises, restricting the flexibility of enterprises' capital operations, and hindering the cultivation and growth of enterprises' long-term value. Based on the theories of corporate finance, information asymmetry, and transaction costs, this paper deeply analyzes the internal logic of how fintech enables the upgrading of enterprises' investment and financing, and also outlines the specific paths for its implementation. Leveraging the technological advantages of digitalization and intelligence, fintech has broken through the time and space limitations and mode barriers of traditional financial services, effectively expanding the financing channels for enterprises, avoiding subjective human biases in investment decisions, and effectively alleviating the financing difficulties commonly faced by small and medium-sized enterprises. It continuously optimizes the allocation efficiency of capital in the market. However, during the process of industrial implementation, the deep integration of fintech and the real economy still faces numerous obstacles. Problems such as uneven digital literacy among market entities, imperfect data governance systems of financial institutions, technical loopholes in algorithm models, and lagging iterations of industry regulatory systems all to some extent weaken the enabling efficacy of digital finance. In response to these practical challenges, this paper builds a collaborative optimization framework involving enterprises, financial institutions, and regulatory authorities, providing effective theoretical support and practical references for digital finance to deeply penetrate the real economy and empower industrial development, and helping real enterprises achieve stable and high-quality long-term development.

title: Geopolitical risk and export competitiveness: evidence from BRICS and Asian economies using CS-ARDL, difference-in-differences and MMQR approaches
summary: Purpose This study aims to assess the effect of geopolitical risk (GPR) on export competitiveness for 15 Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa and Asian economies during the 1990–2024, combining long-run, quasi-causal and distributional evidence. It looks as if increased geopolitical uncertainty impacts countries’ comparative advantage, and how these impacts may differ between economies of varying export competitiveness. Design/methodology/approach The revealed comparative advantage (RCA) index is used to measure export competitiveness. The analysis includes three complementary econometric techniques: cross-sectionally augmented autoregressive distributed lag (ARDL) to estimate long run relations in presence of cross-sectional dependence, Difference-in-Differences (DiD) with event-study framework to capture the causal effect of major geopolitical shocks and method of moments quantile regression (MMQR) to capture the heterogeneous impacts across the conditional distributions of export competitiveness. Findings The direct short-run relationship between GPR and export competitiveness is negative and statistically significant across the pooled two-way fixed-effects and MMQR specifications, whereas the cross-sectionally augmented autoregressive distributed lag long-run mean-group coefficient for the full panel is small and not statistically distinguishable from zero, concealing substantial cross-country heterogeneity that only the country-specific and distributional estimates reveal. The DiD and a supplementary triple-difference Difference-in-Difference-in-Differences (Triple Differences) (DDD) test find no statistically significant differential shift in competitiveness for high-GPR economies immediately around the 2014 or 2022 shock windows, but the direct GPR elasticity remains negative and significant net of these treatment effects. The most novel evidence comes from MMQR: the GPR coefficient is strongly negative at the lower quantiles of the RCA distribution and turns positive at the upper quantiles, indicating that GPR disproportionately damages the weakest exporters while leaving the most competitive economies largely unaffected or, in resource-exporting cases, marginally better off. Originality/value This study is unique and valuable to the international trade and political economy literature for its quasi-experimental evidence bearing on the causal channel through which GPR affects trade, by country, using a multi-method empirical approach. The study combines long-run, causal and distributional analyses to provide new insights into the geopolitical uncertainty’s impact on export competitiveness and the importance of bolstering supply chain resilience, export diversification and institutional capacity to buffer geopolitical shocks.

title: Environmental Reporting and Firm Value in the Manufacturing Firms in Nigeria
summary: This study examined the adoption of the independent audit profession to the digital era, focusing on how Computer-Assisted Audit Techniques (CAATs), audit software, cloud-based systems, and auditors’ data analytics skills influence audit efficiency. The research adopted an ex-post facto design and obtained data from selected organizations through questionnaires, observation, and secondary sources. Descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and simple linear regression were used to analyze the data. Findings revealed that all four digital-audit variables have significant positive effects on audit efficiency. Auditors’ data analytics skills had the strongest influence on audit outcomes, followed closely by CAATs and audit software, indicating that analytical competency and automation are central to digital-era auditing. Cloud-based systems also contributed positively, though to a lesser extent, reflecting challenges associated with cybersecurity concerns and infrastructural limitations. The model explained 64.2% of the variation in audit efficiency, and all null hypotheses were rejected. The study concludes that digital adoption is essential for maintaining audit quality, relevance, and professional competitiveness in a rapidly evolving technological environment. It recommends enhanced training in data analytics, increased deployment of CAATs and audit software, improved cloud security frameworks, and updated regulatory standards to support full digital integration within the audit profession.

title: Financial Management, Accounting Training, and Financial Technology as Determinants of Microenterprise Financial Performance
summary: Financial performance is central to the sustainability of microenterprises, yet their ability to achieve favorable financial outcomes may be associated with how effectively financial activities are managed, the accounting training received by business owners, and the utilization of financial technology. This study examined the relationships between financial management, accounting training, financial technology, and the financial performance of microenterprises in Medan Labuhan District, Medan, Indonesia. A quantitative explanatory cross-sectional design was employed involving 100 microenterprise owners selected through simple random sampling. Data were collected using a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4.0. The results showed that financial management was positively and significantly associated with financial performance (β = .308), accounting training demonstrated a positive and significant association with financial performance (β = .331), and financial technology was also positively and significantly associated with financial performance (β = .226). Among the three predictors, accounting training showed the largest path coefficient in the structural model. Collectively, financial management, accounting training, and financial technology explained 54.7% of the variance in microenterprise financial performance (R² = .547), while 45.3% of the variance remained unexplained by the model. The Q²predict value of .521 further indicated predictive relevance for the endogenous construct. These findings provide context-specific evidence that financial management, accounting training, and financial technology utilization are relevant to explaining microenterprise financial performance, with accounting training showing the strongest relative association within the examined structural model.

title: LEVERAGING FINTECH FOR SUSTAINABLE SUPPLY CHAINS: THE ROLES OF ORGANIZATIONAL CAPABILITIES AND ENVIRONMENTAL UNCERTAINTY IN SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES
summary: The purpose of the study is to analyse the factors affecting green supply chain management (GSCM) within small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), with respect to the adoption of Fintech, organisational capabilities, and the impact of environmental uncertainty. It aims to provide information on how digital tools and internal resources can be used to promote sustainable supply chain practices and help firms respond effectively to a dynamic market environment. A self-administered survey of SME entrepreneurs was used to collect data, which were analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) to test direct, mediating, and moderating relationships. The findings show that the adoption of Fintech can have a significant positive or indirect impact on GSCM through IT capability, supply chain transparency, and the adoption of green technology. Environmental uncertainty moderates the positive relationship between IT capability and green technology adoption and the negative relationship between supply chain transparency and GSCM. These results indicate that digital finance and organisational capabilities are more effective at fostering sustainable supply chains when aligned with the external environmental context. The research builds upon the Resource-Based View and Contingency Theory by showing that fintech adoption is a strategic digital resource whose effectiveness in enhancing GSCM depends on internal capacity and the environment, thereby providing a comprehensive picture of the mechanisms for operating sustainable supply chain management and its boundary conditions. It is recommended that managers strategically implement fintech solutions, develop IT and green technology capacity, and balance transparency programs in response to environmental uncertainty, and that policymakers promote SME sustainability by supporting fintech implementation and the adoption of adaptive green technologies.

title: Research on the Impact, Mechanism and Heterogeneity of Financial Technology on the Operations of Commercial Banks
summary: FinTech refers to the new business model, application, process and product formed after digital technology enters the financial services sector. This article distinguishes between the external shock caused by the entry of FinTech enterprises into traditional financial markets and the internal transformation carried out by commercial banks through the application of digital technology. It examines the impact of FinTech on the operations of commercial banks from three aspects: profitability, risk-taking and business structure, and analyzes three transmission mechanisms: information asymmetry, market competition and liquidity creation. The research shows that the external development of FinTech will divert bank deposits, payment services and credit customers, putting pressure on traditional income; after banks apply digital technology to customer identification, credit approval and internal operations, they can reduce information processing costs and expand service scope. FinTech helps to reduce the credit risk of individual banks, while deposit competition, profit constraints, model convergence and enhanced inter-bank connections may increase risk-taking or expand systemic risks. These impacts vary with bank size, property rights and business model, as well as the level of digital infrastructure and technology application in the region. Regulatory authorities need to implement classified supervision based on the source of technology, bank type and risk level, while commercial banks should choose a transformation path that is compatible with their customer base and technical capabilities.

title: The Impact of Corporate Governance on Enhancing Environmental Sustainability: An Applied Study on the Saudi Energy Sector
summary: This study aims to analyse the impact of corporate governance on enhancing environmental sustainability and its reflection on financial performance in the Saudi energy sector during the period (2020–2024), within the framework of the modern orientations of Saudi Vision 2030 toward sustainable development and the promotion of governance practices and environmental disclosure، The study focuses on examining the relationship between corporate governance mechanisms, represented by board size, board independence, and the number of annual board meetings, and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) practices, in addition to measuring the impact of sustainability on firms’ financial performance. The study adopted a descriptive and applied analytical approach using secondary data extracted from the Bloomberg platform at the College of Business Administration, Majmaah University، Multiple regression analysis was conducted using the SPSS program to test the study hypotheses، The study sample included six leading companies in the Saudi energy sector: Saudi Aramco, Petro Rabigh, Saudi Arabian Refineries Company, Arabian Drilling, ADES Holding, and Bahri. The findings revealed a statistically significant impact of corporate governance mechanisms on environmental sustainability practices، Board independence was found to have a positive effect on the level of sustainability implementation, whereas board size showed a negative effect on sustainability indicators due to increased administrative complexity and slower decision-making processes، The results also indicated a positive relationship between cash liquidity and the adoption of sustainability practices، Furthermore, the study found a statistically significant impact of ESG practices on financial performance measured by Return on Assets (ROA), confirming the importance of sustainability as a supporting factor for operational efficiency and long-term value creation.

title: PENGARUH KEPEMILIKAN MANAJERIAL, PROFITABILITAS DAN LEVERAGE TERHADAP MANAJEMEN LABA DENGAN KUALITAS AUDIT SEBAGAI VARIABEL MODERASI
summary: Earnings management refers to managerial actions in adjusting reported earnings to achieve certain objectives. This study examines the effects of managerial ownership, profitability, and leverage on earnings management, with audit quality as a moderating variable, in mining companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during 2018–2022. Secondary data were obtained from the companies’ financial reports. Purposive sampling selected 152 observations. The analysis included descriptive statistics, classical assumption tests, multiple linear regression (MLR), t-tests, F-tests, and the coefficient of determination (R²). The findings indicate that managerial ownership and profitability negatively affect earnings management, while leverage has a positive effect. Audit quality does not moderate the effects of managerial ownership or leverage on earnings management. However, audit quality strengthens the effect of profitability on earnings management. This study provides a better understanding of how companies use strategies to manipulate financial reporting to achieve certain objectives.

title: Beyond the Styrofoam Tray: A Practical Sustainability Roadmap for Union Supermarket, a Family-Owned Grocer in Providence
summary: Union Supermarket Providence is a family-owned business in Providence, Rhode Island, that operates a meat market, a mini grocery store and a restaurant. This article presents the corporate social responsibility (CSR) plan developed for the company with reference to the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) Standards. The diagnosis identifies four pressure points: heavy reliance on single-use packaging (plastic wrap and Styrofoam trays in the meat department); a waste system with no composting and no measurement of volumes, at a cost of $3,773 per month; high energy demand from refrigeration and lighting; and an emissions-intensive meat supply chain. The plan proposes five prioritised initiatives on a four-month timetable — a food donation programme, a "Wonky Produce" section, participation in surplus-food apps such as Too Good To Go, pre-consumer composting and a food waste tracking tool — followed by sustainable packaging, energy efficiency upgrades and rooftop solar in the medium to long term. The plan’s estimates, which are projections rather than results, include diverting 25–40% of food waste from landfill, cutting energy consumption by 20–30%, saving $15,000–20,000 a year on electricity with a two-to-three-year payback, and avoiding 15–20 tonnes of CO2 equivalent annually. The central lesson for managers of small food retailers is that measurement must precede ambition: without baseline data, neither targets nor return on investment can be verified.

title: Corporate Social Responsibility as a Business Strategy for the Survival and Sustainability of Migrant Entrepreneurs
summary: ABSTRACT Migrant entrepreneurs operating in host‐country markets face xenophobia, capital exclusion, and institutional discrimination that threaten basic business survival, yet this context remains theoretically underspecified. Existing research frames CSR as an optional legitimacy tool in stable, developed‐country settings, overlooking contexts where institutional protection is absent. Drawing on Stakeholder Theory, Legitimacy Theory, and the Resource‐Based View, the present study interprets the concept of corporate social responsibility (CSR) as manifesting, in the participants' accounts, as a strategy oriented towards survival rather than as a discretionary legitimacy tool and introduces moral capital as an institutional substitute in developing‐country migrant entrepreneurship. Using an exploratory qualitative design, 21 in‐depth interviews were conducted with migrant‐owned businesses in Türkiye; inductive content analysis revealed four CSR dimensions: employee‐oriented, customer‐oriented, societal, and environmental. The findings suggest that, in these participants' narratives, CSR operates less as a discretionary strategy and more as a central means through which market access, legitimacy, and resilience are pursued under structural scarcity. These findings represent an interpretive extension of the existing CSR (Corporate Social Responsibility) theoretical framework, proposing that within such contexts, CSR may function more closely as a survival‐oriented mechanism than as a reputational option.

title: Reflections on Remote Audit Practice in Accounting Firms
summary: The audit profession has long been advancing the development of informatization and intelligent systems. As an important exploration of the digital transformation of the industry, remote auditing was comprehensively tested during the special period of the COVID-19 pandemic. Accounting firms that operate under explicit business deadlines, facing the enormous impact of the pandemic, made every effort to reduce the disruption to their engagements by using various remote technologies and means. Judged by the implementation results, remote audit technology has substituted only part of on-site auditing and is still constrained by many factors; the submission and disclosure of the 2019 audit reports were delayed to a certain extent. This has also triggered deep reflection within the industry on the application and deployment of digital information technology. On this basis, this paper starts from the audit engagements and the status of technology application of accounting firms during the pandemic, and attempts to provide more insights for the optimization of remote auditing and the digital and intelligent upgrading of the audit profession.

title: PENGARUH AKUNTANSI MANAJEMEN LINGKUNGAN, BIAYA LINGKUNGAN, DAN PENGUNGKAPAN EMISI GAS RUMAH KACA TERHADAP NILAI PERUSAHAAN
summary: This study aims to analyze the effect of Environmental Management Accounting (EMA), environmental costs, and greenhouse gas (GHG) emission disclosures on firm value. The population of this study comprises basic and chemical industry manufacturing companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) for the 2021–2025 period. A purposive sampling technique was employed, resulting in a sample of 43 companies. Using multiple linear regression analysis via SPSS 25, the results demonstrate that EMA and GHG emission disclosures have a positive effect on firm value, whereas environmental costs show no significant effect. The Adjusted R2 value of 41.4% indicates that these three independent variables explain 41.4% of the variation in firm value, with the remaining 58.6% attributable to factors outside the model Implicatively, corporate management can utilize EMA and GHG disclosures as strategic communication instruments to send positive signals to the market in order to enhance firm value. Future research is encouraged to examine additional variables beyond those included in this study, expand the sector coverage, and extend the observation period to obtain a more comprehensive insight. title: A Supply Chain Ecosystem Approach to Smart City Manufacturing Clusters: Digital Transformation-Enabled Energy Management in Urban Water Systems
summary: This study develops a supply chain ecosystem (SCE) approach for smart city manufacturing clusters (SCMCs) through the integration of digital technologies into energy management of urban water systems (UWSs). The proposed framework integrates the Internet of Things (IoT), blockchain, and machine learning (ML) analytics within a smart water grid architecture to support sustainable and energy-efficient water supply management. Its principal contribution is an SCE-oriented information and analytical framework linking distributed system entities and stakeholders through integrated data management and decision support. To address the hierarchical and multi-objective nature of the energy management problem, a stratified representation approach is proposed, enabling decomposition into interconnected subproblems and improving coordination across multiple system levels within the SCE. An information-analytical system is developed, integrating subsystems for data acquisition, processing, storage, analysis, planning, monitoring, and decision support. The proposed architecture combines IoT-enabled real-time data acquisition with blockchain-based mechanisms supporting data integrity, traceability, and verifiable information exchange among system entities. Energy planning is formalised through the construction of an energy baseline (EnB) accounting for system hierarchy, operational constraints, and planning horizon. The operational application of the framework is demonstrated using a case study of a water intake facility. GMDH (Group Method of Data Handling) neural networks are applied to model energy consumption, while multi-criteria analysis identifies a second-order polynomial activation function as optimal, achieving high predictive accuracy (MAPE = 0.513%; RMSPE = 0.595%). The resulting day-ahead EnB, based on planned technological parameters and pump operation schedules, demonstrates how the proposed SCE framework translates integrated data management into operational decision support for energy-efficient UWS operation.

title: The Impact of Digital Transformation on the Cost of Equity
summary: In the context of the digital era, the rapid development of computers and information technology has brought profound changes to the operating environment of enterprises, creating broad opportunities while also presenting a series of challenges that require urgent responses. Against this backdrop, digital transformation has gradually become a strategic focus for enterprises seeking to capitalize on emerging opportunities and effectively address these challenges. This study empirically examines listed companies in the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock markets from 2014 to 2023. The results show that corporate digital transformation significantly reduces the cost of equity. Specifically, digital transformation can reduce the cost of equity by mitigating information asymmetry and improving the corporate governance environment. Further analysis reveals that the negative effect of digital transformation on the cost of equity is more pronounced among firms located in eastern China and those with overconfident executives. Based on these findings, this study proposes several recommendations to promote corporate digital transformation and help enterprises implement digital transformation more effectively, thereby enhancing their competitiveness in the market.

title: The Impact of Stock Liquidity on Corporate ESG : Which Industry Benefits?
summary: ABSTRACT Considering the role of capital market governance in guiding corporate green transformation under the goal of environmental protection, this paper aims to empirically study the impact of stock liquidity on corporate ESG based on the data of listed companies in China from 2009 to 2021. The empirical results indicate that stock liquidity exerts a positive impact on the overall corporate ESG and the three specific dimensions, such as environmental performance, social responsibility, and corporate governance. Furthermore, empirical evidence suggests that stock liquidity can positively affect the ESG performance by inducing green technology innovation and improving managerial shareholding. Finally, the results for heterogeneity indicate that stock liquidity's positive impact on corporate ESG varies among different firms, which is stronger in heavily polluting industries, competitive industries, and western regions. By alleviating the influence of stock liquidity on corporate ESG performance, this study provides certain policy implications for promoting green transformation.

title: The Impact of Accounting Conservatism on Earnings Management, the Moderating Role of Capital Ownership Structures - Empirical Evidence in Vietnam
summary: Purpose: This study aims to extend the existing literature by empirically examining the influence of accounting conservatism on earnings management in the Vietnamese context. In particular, this study also investigates how ownership structures moderate the relationship between conservative accounting and earnings management. Methodology: A multivariate regression model on a sample of 1,075 firm-year observations of 215 companies listed on HOSE or HNX from 2019 to 2023 was employed. In this study, we used panel data to test the hypotheses. Furthermore, firm size, financial leverage, and audit firm type were used as control variables. Findings: The findings shed light on the negative relationship between accounting conservatism and earnings management in the Vietnamese context. Overall, accounting conservatism still plays a positive informational role in Vietnam’s financial statements in this manner. The findings also reveal that large shareholder ownership strengthens the negative effect of accounting conservatism on earnings management, while managerial ownership and state ownership weaken this relationship. Research limitations/implications: Our findings provide important implications for companies, users of financial statements, and accounting standards setters to consider the impact of accounting conservatism on earnings management, which results in high-quality earnings reported in the financial statements. Originality/value: The study further contributes to the scholarly literature by examining whether and how ownership structures moderate the relationship between accounting conservatism and earnings management, thereby addressing the existing research gap and offering additional insights into the conflicting findings of previous research.

summary: This study aims to analyse the findings of previous research on the impact of the implementation of corporate social responsibility, good corporate governance and financial performance on firm value in telecommunications companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange for the period 2021–2026. This study employs a literature review method using a descriptive qualitative approach. Literature was collected using the Publish or Perish application, involving 15 relevant journal articles. The analysis was conducted by identifying the variables, methods, subjects and research findings, and then comparing the findings to determine trends in the relationships between variables. The results of the study indicate that the influence of CSR, GCG and financial performance on firm value still shows mixed results. CSR tends to have a positive influence, whilst GCG and financial performance yield varying results, ranging from positive, negative to no effect. These differing findings suggest that the relationships between variables may be influenced by firm characteristics, industry sector, the research period and the indicators used.

title: Regional digital finance and food supply-chain management resilience: evidence on the regional-to-firm conversion gap in China’s emerging listed food enterprises
summary: Food supply chains face climate shocks, logistics disruption, food-safety incidents and volatile demand, yet the relevance of regional digital finance for firm-level resilience remains uncertain. This study examines the association between a province-level digital-finance environment and an accounting-based food supply-chain resilience proxy among emerging listed food enterprises in China. Using public data for 122 eligible firms, we construct annual resistance, recovery and stability measures from revenue, operating cash flow and net margin; the common two-way fixed-effects sample contains 732 firm-year observations from 119 firms during 2017–2023. Regional digital finance is measured as a province-level external financial environment rather than firm-level digital transformation or adoption. Operational capability and regional consumption capacity are accounting- and province-level proxies and do not directly observe supplier coordination, traceability, cold-chain performance, or product-level demand. The preferred estimate is close to zero [beta = −0.005, SE = 0.063, 95% CI (−0.128, 0.117)]. Alternative covariance estimators, outcome definitions and timing specifications do not establish a stable positive within-firm association. The proxy-based operational-capability pathway and the conditional consumption-capacity association are likewise not established. Equivalence tests at 0.05 and 0.10 SCR-standard-deviation bounds are not significant, and the approximate 80% minimum detectable effect is 1.575 SCR standard deviations. The evidence therefore cannot distinguish a small contextual association from limited within-firm statistical precision. The findings support a bounded regional-to-firm conversion interpretation: regional finance may widen resource availability, but whether it is associated with resilience depends on unobserved operational conversion routines and food-sector coordination conditions.

title: Integration of Islamic Crowdfunding, Cash Waqf, and Islamic Microfinance for Poverty Alleviation in Ethiopia
summary: This paper's underlying aim is to design a strategy to develop an integrated Islamic-Crowdfunding-Cash-Waqf (ICFCW) Model for adopting IsMF services. Besides, it focused on exploring new channels for Islamic social finance towards fundraising with the employment of financial technology (FinTech). FinTech plays a central role in access to financial services and its use nowadays. This research targeted poverty alleviation by channeling funds through Islamic crowdfunding and cash waqf financial instruments for IsMFIs. Moreover, examining and validating the viability of the ICFCW model in Ethiopia is another focus of this study. Regarding the research methodology, a mixed-method design was employed. In particular, semi-structured interviews were conducted and analyzed using thematic analysis, and a case study was applied using the snowball sampling method. Accordingly, the analyzed survey data from the pilot case study revealed that the ICFCW model (equity-based financing) was ranked third, following PLS-based financing (Musharakah and Mudarabah) and Murabahah -based financing, which were ranked first and second, respectively. Additionally, the thematic analysis results show that the study findings, supported by many respondents, indicate a preference for the ICFCW model due to its novel approach to resource mobilization and its role as an alternative financial instrument, despite the low level of awareness of crowdfunding and cash waqf in the country. Thus, crowdfunding, particularly Islamic crowdfunding, is a relatively new concept in the Ethiopian financial industry. However, it has recently become popular for donation-based (charity) campaigns and is rapidly growing through social media platforms.

title: Diversity of fauna and flora in the areas around the Kura River
summary: The Kura River and its riparian corridor support a mosaic of aquatic, riverbank and floodplain habitats that provide living space for plants, fish, birds, amphibians, reptiles, insects and small mammals. This study develops an original school research project into a structured academic assessment of fauna and flora diversity around the Kura River. The source project used observation, photographs, maps and online and book-based research to classify representative organisms and compare biodiversity among in-water, riverbank and nearby-land habitats. The student identified reeds, grasses, algae, willow trees, aquatic plants and shrubs together with fish, frogs, turtles, birds, insects and small mammals, and prepared descriptive tables, a classification chart, seasonal river photographs and a river-course map. These materials are retained in the present article as the primary source evidence. The findings indicate that habitat heterogeneity is central to biodiversity: aquatic and riverbank zones were classified as high-diversity environments, while nearby land was classified as medium-high. Pollution, plastic and other waste, removal of riverside vegetation, habitat modification and inefficient water use were identified as principal threats. Recent Kura research supports the importance of water quality, riparian vegetation and ecosystem restoration. The discussion further links biodiversity conservation to ecosystem services, blue-green tourism, nature-based solutions and green finance. The study concludes that protecting the Kura requires integrated water-quality management, riparian restoration, waste prevention, environmental education and systematic biodiversity monitoring.

title: A Case Study of the E-commerce Major Serving Intangible Cultural Heritage Inheritance in Tibetan Areas: Taking Gansu Minzu Normal University as an Example
summary: The living inheritance of intangible cultural heritage (ICH) bears an inherent coupling relationship with rural cultural revitalization in ethnic minority areas, and e-commerce is increasingly serving as a novel channel connecting ICH resources in Tibetan regions with external markets and youth populations. Taking the Ecommerce major at Gansu Minzu Normal University, situated in Gannan Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, as a case study, this paper draws on secondary data from university official websites, government public materials, and published scholarship to examine how an applied undergraduate program engages in ICH inheritance through four pathways: talent cultivation, practical training platforms, faculty-student teams, and university-local cooperation. The study finds that the program has preliminarily established a fourdimensional linkage framework of resources–actors–platforms–institutions, and has manifested an institutional awareness of serving cultural development in Tibetan areas across live-streaming training, competition-based education, and university-local negotiations. Nevertheless, persistent shortcomings remain, including shallow integration between the program and ICH, a shortage of bilingual and interdisciplinary faculty, weak standardization and supply chains for ICH products, tension between cultural authenticity and commercialization, and an absence of sustainable mechanisms. Accordingly, this paper proposes countermeasures encompassing deepened curriculum embedding, co-construction of faculty teams and workshops, improved supply chains and branding, and the establishment of authenticity review and long-term cooperation mechanisms, so as to provide transferable lessons for e-commerce programs in comparable universities in ethnic minority regions to support ICH inheritance.

title: Metaverse and NFT-Based Digital Ecosystems: Sustainability, Governance, and Energy Trade-Offs
summary: Metaverse platforms and non-fungible token (NFT) markets are often framed as immaterial, frictionless layers of the digital economy. However, their expansion depends on energy-intensive infrastructures, complex governance arrangements, and regulatory choices that can amplify or mitigate environmental externalities. This article examines sustainability, governance, and energy trade-offs in metaverse and NFT-based ecosystems. The research treats China as a policy and regulatory laboratory. This is to explore the ideas of how "digital collectibles" and platform-based experiments have evolved under tighter constraints on cryptocurrency circulation. Building on a socio-technical perspective, the paper connects three levels of analysis. It maps the material footprint of immersive experiences and tokenized assets, focusing on consensus mechanisms, cloud and data center dependencies, and the risk of rebound effects. The exploration of governance addresses technical standards and platform accountability. In the meantime, it discusses the tensions between openness, interoperability, and enforceable rules. A comparison of regulatory pathways addresses their implications for sustainability metrics, user rights, and market design. The contribution of this research lies in the framework for evaluating whether metaverse and NFT ecosystems can credibly align with sustainability goals without relying on rhetorical "green" narratives. This research also proposes governance levers that make environmental accounting and accountability operational rather than aspirational. title: Applications of Artificial Intelligence in Managerial Decision-Making for Sustainable Agro-Export Operations in Latin America: A Systematic Review and Bibliometric Analysis, 1996-2025
summary: Background Artificial intelligence is transforming agro-export management by converting production, commercial, climate, and logistics data into support for more timely decisions. In Latin America, however, evidence on its managerial applications and contribution to sustainable operations remains fragmented. Objective To synthesize evidence on the application of artificial intelligence to managerial decision-making and its contribution to the efficiency, sustainability, traceability, resilience, and competitiveness of sustainable agro-export operations in Latin America from 1996 to 2025. Methods A systematic review and bibliometric analysis were conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020. Scopus and Web of Science yielded 2160 records; after filtering, screening, and eligibility assessment, 73 studies were included. Bibliometrix in RStudio and VOSviewer were used to analyze scientific production, authors, countries, sources, Bradford’s and Lotka’s laws, keyword co-occurrence, and thematic clusters. Results Scientific output increased markedly after 2021 and peaked in 2024. Scopus accounted for 98.95% of the records. China led with 170 publications, while Brazil, with 149, was the only Latin American country among the five most productive. Four thematic areas were identified: prediction and classification using artificial intelligence and machine learning; logistics, supply chains, and suppliers; sustainable resource management and climate risks; and digital transformation through Agriculture 4.0/5.0. Across the literature, artificial intelligence was found to reduce uncertainty and improve decision-making, although its effectiveness depends on data quality, digital infrastructure, and organizational capabilities. Conclusions Artificial intelligence represents a strategic capability for strengthening sustainable agro-export operations. Its impact depends on integrating algorithms with reliable data, technological infrastructure, organizational capabilities, and sustainability criteria. The limited representation of Latin America highlights the need for further empirical research adapted to regional conditions.

title: Effect of Board Characteristics on Voluntary Disclosures of Listed Commercial Banks in Nigeria
summary: This study examines the effect of board characteristics on voluntary disclosures in listed commercial banks in Nigeria, utilizing a longitudinal research design and dynamic panel regression with the Generalized Method of Moments (GMM) for analysis. The study covers a period from 2014 to 2023, focusing on 15 banks listed on the Nigerian Exchange Group (NGX). Key board characteristics investigated include board financial expertise, independence, gender diversity, and the presence of foreign directors, alongside financial metrics such as profitability and leverage. The findings reveal that board financial expertise, independence, and the presence of foreign directors significantly enhance voluntary disclosures. In contrast, board gender diversity does not exhibit a significant impact on disclosure levels, while profitability shows no meaningful relationship, and financial leverage is positively associated with voluntary disclosures. Based on the findings, recommendations are made for banks should prioritize appointing directors with financial expertise, such as accounting, auditing, or finance backgrounds. These individuals can play a pivotal role in promoting high-quality financial reporting and voluntary disclosures, thereby enhancing transparency and stakeholder trust.

summary: This research aimed to examine corporate governance, liquidity management and profitability affecting investment decisions in listed companies on the Stock Exchange of Thailand in the SET ESG index, classifying investment decisions into three dimensions: earnings per share, stock price and price change rate. Secondary data were collected from financial statements, Form 56-1 One Report, the Corporate Governance Report of Thai Listed Companies, and the corporate-action adjusted stock price database during 2023–2025, comprising 62 companies and 186 firm-year observations. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, correlation analysis and multiple regression. As the data constitute a panel, a robustness check was additionally performed using panel regression models selected by the Hausman test with firm-clustered robust standard errors. The results revealed that profitability significantly affected investment decisions at the 0.01 level in all three dimensions (earnings per share F = 8.108, R² = 0.152; stock price F = 7.707, R² = 0.146; price change rate F = 4.981, R² = 0.099). Return on equity positively affected earnings per share and stock price, while gross profit margin positively affected earnings per share. Corporate governance affected earnings per share through board meeting frequency and stock price through board size, whereas liquidity management affected only stock price (F = 3.577, R² = 0.038). The corporate governance rating showed no significant effect because 61 of 62 companies (98.39 percent) received the highest rating. The robustness check indicated that the findings on profitability for earnings per share and price change rate, and on liquidity management for stock price, remained robust, whereas those on corporate governance and on profitability for stock price were not robust. The value of this research lies in the empirical confirmation that, even among companies with high sustainability standards, profitability and cash-conversion efficiency remain decisive factors influencing investment decisions, while also demonstrating the importance of verifying the robustness of results when using panel data. The findings benefit investors in selecting securities, executives and boards in structuring governance mechanisms and managing working capital, and regulators in refining corporate governance assessment criteria.

title: Research on the Impact of Institutional Investor Exit Threats on Management Tone Manipulation
summary: With the continuous development of China's capital market, textual information in annual reports has increasingly become an important channel for investors to understand a firm's development prospects. As the most valuable part of textual information disclosure in annual reports, the Management Discussion and Analysis (MD&A) section, owing to its high subjectivity, provides room for management to manipulate tone. Using Chinese A-share listed firms on the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges from 2007 to 2024 as the research sample, this paper examines the impact of institutional investor exit threats on management tone manipulation. The results show that institutional investor exit threats significantly curb management tone manipulation, and this conclusion still holds after robustness tests including the replacement of the dependent variable, the instrumental variable method, propensity score matching, and the Heckman two-stage model. Mechanism tests indicate that exit threats inhibit tone manipulation by constraining managers' self-serving behavior and improving corporate information transparency. Further analysis reveals that the governance effect of exit threats is stronger in state-owned enterprises, in firms located in regions with a lower degree of marketization, and in firms with lower Type II agency costs, and that exit threats can enhance firm value by curbing tone manipulation. This paper extends the research on the governance effect of exit threats and on management tone manipulation, and provides implications for regulators, listed firms, and investors.

title: Financial Inclusion or Digital Discrimination? Algorithmic Credit Decisions and Gender Inequalities: A Scoping Review
summary: The rapid expansion of financial technologies has repositioned algorithmic credit decision systems as central gatekeepers of economic opportunity, raising a fundamental sociological question: Do these systems broaden financial inclusion or do they reproduce—and potentially amplify—gender inequalities under a veneer of technical neutrality? This scoping review maps the scientific literature at the intersection of algorithmic credit decisions, financial inclusion, and gender, following the PRISMA-ScR protocol and combining bibliometric and thematic analysis. A corpus of 279 peer-reviewed documents (English-language articles and reviews, 2022–2026) indexed in Scopus was charted, exhibiting a compound annual growth rate of 31.6%, 4445 accumulated citations (h-index = 32), and a highly skewed citation distribution (Gini = 0.819). Production is led by the Global South—India (n = 64), Indonesia (n = 32), and South Africa (n = 19)—while co-word and semantic cluster analysis reveals five research fronts organized around digital financial literacy, gender and banking, artificial intelligence and blockchain, microfinance and the Sustainable Development Goals, and algorithmic risk assessment. The gender-focused subcorpus (n = 58; 20.8%) and the algorithmic credit subcorpus (n = 49; 17.6%) intersect in only 11 documents (3.9%), exposing a critical research gap precisely where the promise of inclusion and the risk of discrimination collide. This overlap is no larger than independence would predict (expected = 10.2; Fisher’s exact p = 0.85) and stays below 5% under alternative tagging dictionaries, while documents authored exclusively by Global South institutions receive 44% fewer citations than comparable documents. Evidence charted from the corpus documents both inclusionary effects (expanded access for thin-file borrowers, reduced transaction costs) and exclusionary dynamics (gender-miscalibrated credit scores, predatory digital lending, algorithmic opacity, and intersectional data gaps). Rurality, informal employment, ethnicity, and migration status are rarely analyzed together with gender, and an integrative conceptual model links structural conditions, intersecting social positions, data regimes, and algorithmic pipelines to inclusionary, predatory, and exclusionary outcomes. The review proposes an agenda oriented toward algorithmic auditing with gender-disaggregated data, regulatory frameworks for fairness in credit scoring, and the integration of feminist data perspectives into fintech design, arguing that financial inclusion and digital discrimination are not mutually exclusive outcomes but coexisting logics of the same socio-technical infrastructure.
