title: Spatio-temporal variation and determinants of urban air quality in Chinese cities during 2014-2023: an interpretable machine learning analysis
summary: China launched its clean-air action plans in 2013, which have played a crucial role in driving one of the world's most significant and rapid improvements in urban air quality. However, the relative roles of financial, governance, and structural determinants remain poorly understood. This study developed a national-scale, interpretable machine-learning framework to model and explain air quality dynamics across 273 prefecture-level cities from 2014 to 2023. We used city-level AQI as the target variable and assembled a multidimensional panel of socioeconomic, financial, technological, energy, and governance indicators. We fitted a TPE-tuned XGBoost model and interpreted it using SHAP (global and local attributions) and ALE (non-linear response curves and two-way interactions). Nationally, more than 85% of cities exhibit substantial AQI declines, but improvements are uneven across regions and provinces. SHAP results identify green finance, population density, government intervention, openness, and digital finance as the most influential determinants, with energy consumption, green technology innovation, foreign direct investment, industrial structure, and urbanization also playing important roles. ALE analysis reveals strong nonlinearities: green and digital finance, as well as government intervention, are pollution-increasing at low and intermediate levels but become markedly pollution-reducing beyond critical thresholds, while density and energy use rapidly become strong positive drivers once modest levels are exceeded. Interactions show that green and digital finance yield significant air-quality benefits only when combined with strong governance and less energy-intensive and industry-intensive structures. City-level decompositions further distinguish improving from deteriorating cities in terms of the evolution of these drivers. The findings highlight that sustained governance, well-targeted green and digital finance, and accelerated structural change are mutually necessary to secure durable gains in urban air quality.

title: The Impact of "Flow Thought" from an Ownership Perspective on Corporate Performance
summary: Corporate performance, a core indicator of microeconomic vitality, affects employment, tax revenue, high-quality development. Limited academic work explores how "flow thought," understood through its own theoretical meaning, shapes corporate performance. This paper uses the resource-based view, draws on Shanghai-Shenzhen A-share listed firms from 2021 to 2024, empirically tests "flow thought" effects on corporate performance (Return on Assets, ROA), ownership structure's heterogeneous influence. Results show "flow thought" significantly improves corporate performance. This effect appears only in state-owned enterprises; non-state-owned firms show no significant effect. Robustness tests, endogeneity analysis support these findings. Ownership structure, an institutional boundary condition, shapes how efficiently "flow thought" becomes performance improvement. The study offers guidance for firms developing differentiated strategies in the digital economy. It helps explain institutional conditions that turn a management idea into measurable firm performance. These results clarify when flow thought works, why ownership matters, how firms can adapt strategies across different institutional settings.

title: Construction of an agricultural green development indicator system and trend projection for the 15th five-year plan period in Jiangxi Province
summary: Introduction As a central pillar of high-quality agricultural advancement, agricultural green development (AGD) is essential for promoting agricultural and rural modernization and building a strong agricultural province. Methods Focusing on Jiangxi Province—a key traditional agricultural province and a national ecological civilization pilot zone—this study establishes a comprehensive AGD evaluation indicator system covering 18 secondary indicators across five dimensions: resource conservation and efficient utilization, environmental governance of production sites, agricultural ecological restoration, green industrial development, and green technological support. The entropy weight method measures Jiangxi’s AGD level from 2010 to 2025, while the GM(1,1) grey model forecasts its trajectory during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026–2030). Results The results show that: (1) Jiangxi’s comprehensive AGD index grew steadily from 11.37 to 80.51, with agricultural ecological restoration carrying the largest weight (29.42); (2) the index is projected to reach 86.97 by 2030; all fitted GM(1,1) models have MAPE below 10%, meeting the Grade I accuracy standard. Discussion Although constraints remain, including inadequate hilly mechanization, limited smallholder green production capacity, and difficult non-point source pollution control, future work should strengthen green resource utilization, deepen production-site governance, improve technological support, and optimize incentives to drive the green transition of smallholders.

title: Spatiotemporal evolution and driving factors of green transformation in resource-based cities of Western China
summary: Western China’s resource-based cities (WRBCs) have characteristics of “resource dependence” and “development lag,” and all resource-based cities will face difficulty accomplishing green transformation (GT). This paper uses 39 samples of WRBCs from 2003 to 2021, identifying the sources of differentiation in GT in WRBCs through the Dagum Gini coefficient, Kernel density function, and spatial Durbin model. Furthermore, we analyze the driving factors and effects of GT. The results show that the overall GT of WRBCs assumes a fluctuating upward tendency. Interregional disparities are the primary source of differentiation in the GT of WRBCs, and absolute differences within the region are generally narrowing. The digital economy (DIG), agglomeration of productive service industries (SEV), urban industrial innovation (UINV), infrastructure level (IL), and GDP can promote GT. DIG and IL produce positive spillover effects promoting the adjacent region’s GT; however, economically developed regions, the siphoning effect occurs, which is adverse to the GT of the adjacent region. The results are still valid after a series of robustness tests. GT has a positive spatial spillover effect, with an effective spillover boundary of 400 km and a peak of 300 km. This study can support the quantitative for promoting GT and balancing regional inequality in resource-based cities.

title: Human-Enabled Digital Accounting and Cultural Amplification for Financial Reporting Performance
summary: This research investigates the influence of digitalization in accounting systems and human resource quality on financial reporting performance, with organizational culture serving as a moderator. A quantitative method was employed through a survey of 157 SMEs in Jakarta that had adopted digital accounting systems, and the data were analyzed using PLS-SEM. The findings show that digitalization of the accounting system positively and significantly affects financial reporting performance (b = 0.136; p = 0.003), while human resource quality also has a positive and significant effect (b = 0.072; p = 0.045). Organizational culture significantly strengthens both relationships, with interaction coefficients of 0.079 (p = 0.009) and 0.085 (p = 0.004), respectively. The model demonstrates strong predictiVe power (Adjusted R2 = 0.831) and acceptable fit (SRMR = 0.076). Sensitivity testing using the conventional three-dimensional, seven-indicator digital accounting systems measurement produced an Adjusted R² of 0.816 and an SRMR of 0.080. The findings highlight the complementary roles of digitalization, human quality, and organizational culture in financial reporting, while extending DSA measurement to five dimensions and twelve indicators. SMEs should integrate digital adoption, employee quality, and an accountability-oriented culture.

title: Research on the Protection of Consumers' Right of Fair Deal in Big Data Differential Pricing
summary: Aimed the rapid growth of the digital economy, major internet platforms increasingly use big data and algorithms for differential pricing. "Big-data-driven price discrimination," as a problematic form of differential pricing, has gradually become widespread. Platforms construct user profiles based on personal information, consumption levels, device models, and browsing history to estimate users' maximum willingness to pay, enabling personalized pricing, or "different prices for different users." This practice undermines substantive fairness in online transactions and seriously infringes upon consumers' right to fair transactions. China has established a basic regulatory framework through laws and regulations including the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests, the Personal Information Protection Law of the People's Republic of China, and the Rules on Price Conduct of Internet Platforms. Yet enforcement lags behind evolving platform practices. Key challenges include: vague legal standards for identifying unlawful pricing, opacity and complexity of algorithmic decision-making, consumers' difficulty meeting evidentiary burdens, and high costs of redress. This paper analyzes how big-data-driven price discrimination operates, identifies gaps and delays in current law through case review, and maps consumer obstacles. It proposes four targeted improvements: refining legal rules to clarify applicable standards, promoting algorithm transparency and strengthening full-process regulation, supporting consumer rights protection and redress, and balancing business efficiency with transactional fairness. The findings provide actionable insights for regulating algorithmic pricing and improving governance in the digital economy.

title: INTEGRATED ASSESSMENT OF COMMERCIAL BANKS' ECONOMIC SECURITY: RISK-BASED EVIDENCE FROM UZBEKISTAN
summary: This study develops and critically evaluates an integrated framework for assessing the economic security of commercial banks in Uzbekistan. Going beyond conventional solvency measures, the proposed framework incorporates internal financial resilience, exposure to external environmental risks, corporate governance, regulatory compliance, and digital and operational threats. The findings suggest that composite economic security ratings can serve as effective tools for risk prioritization when supported by clearly defined indicators, sensitivity analysis, and independently validated early-warning signals.

title: Ranking green finance instruments and finance-linked environmental transition mechanisms within the environmental, social, and governance (ESG) framework: Empirical evidence from Saudi Arabia's petrochemical industry
summary: The petrochemical industry faces increasing pressure to decarbonize due to its high energy intensity, carbon emissions, and environmental footprint. This study evaluates and ranks green finance instruments and finance-linked environmental transition mechanisms within the Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) framework to identify the highest-ranked mechanisms for supporting the sustainable transition of Saudi Arabia's petrochemical industry. A two-stage multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) framework integrating the Analytic Network Process (ANP) and fuzzy Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) was employed to assess six alternatives comprising four green finance instruments and two finance-linked environmental transition mechanisms against three ESG dimensions and fifteen industry-specific sub-criteria. The results show that the Environmental dimension carries the highest priority, followed by Governance and Social, highlighting the importance of measurable environmental outcomes supported by robust governance structures. Among the evaluated alternatives, green tax policies ranked first, followed by green credit mechanisms and investor risk mitigation instruments. The findings suggest that progressive environmental taxation, preferential green lending, and blended-finance mechanisms are better positioned to support industrial decarbonization while limiting abrupt cost pressures during the transition. Furthermore, the effectiveness of green bonds and emission trading systems depends on transparent governance, regulatory compliance, and credible sustainability reporting frameworks. This study provides policy insights for aligning industrial finance with Saudi Vision 2030, the Saudi Green Initiative, and the Kingdom's 2060 net-zero target, while offering a practical decision-support framework for prioritizing sustainable finance in energy-intensive industries.

title: Digital Service Ecosystem for Rural SME Competitiveness Through Smart Agribusiness Transformation
summary: Rural Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs) increasingly face a structural gap between established production capabilities and limited digital capacity to capture market value directly. In rural agribusiness settings, this challenge is compounded by intermediary dependence, uneven digital literacy, and fragmented institutional support. This study examines how a rural entrepreneurial ecosystem can strengthen SME competitiveness through the integration of smart farming, village institutions, market connectivity, and digital transformation in Desa Cibodas, West Java, Indonesia. A sequential explanatory mixed-methods design was employed, combining a survey of 95 agricultural SME actors with qualitative case study analysis based on interviews with 14 key informants and documentary evidence. The findings show that digital adoption readiness, institutional support, and smart farming capability jointly contribute to SME competitiveness, with digital capability emerging as the strongest predictor. Qualitative findings further identify five interconnected themes and show how BUMDes, smart farming, packaging infrastructure, and emerging digital marketplace initiatives interact within a four-layer rural entrepreneurial ecosystem. The study contributes by conceptualizing digital transformation as a connecting ecosystem-level capability that links production and institutional strengths with market-oriented competitiveness. The findings highlight the need for integrated digital marketplace development, stronger BUMDes coordination, and targeted digital capacity building to improve rural SMEs' market autonomy and competitiveness.

title: Do Firms Shield Employees from Risk Shocks? Empirical Evidence from China
summary: This study investigates firm-employee risk-sharing through implicit employment insurance mechanisms within China’s labor market. Leveraging data from Chinese A-share listed firms and employing Double Machine Learning (DML), we document that firms provide significant insurance against unpredictable risk shocks. Specifically, firms offer nearly full insulation against transitory shocks but only partial insurance against persistent ones. Heterogeneity analyses reveal distinct patterns in this risk-sharing. Managers receive substantially stronger job security guarantees compared to rank-and-file employees. Contrary to conventional wisdom, state-owned enterprises do not provide greater employment stability than private firms. Furthermore, family firms offer weaker insurance, attributable to selective corporate social responsibility fulfillment. Critically, employees implicitly accept wage discounts as premiums in exchange for this job security. Although employment insurance strengthens employment rigidity, wage discounts allow firms to flexibly adjust labor input, so they do not bear additional risk from ensuring employees’ job stability. We further identify a significant substitution effect between public unemployment insurance and firm-provided employment insurance: reducing firms’ unemployment insurance contribution burdens incentivizes them to enhance insurance, thereby strengthening employment stability.

title: Digital Finance and Regional Financial Risk: Evidence from Leverage, Default, and Housing-Market Channels in Eastern China
summary: As digital transformation continues to reshape financial intermediation and resource allocation in emerging markets, maintaining regional financial stability has become increasingly important. Using panel data for 88 prefecture-level cities in eastern China from 2011 to 2023, this study examines the relationship between digital finance and regional financial risk using two-way fixed-effects and instrumental-variable models. The results show that greater digital finance usage depth is associated with significantly lower regional financial risk, with the finding supported by multiple robustness and identification checks. Mechanism analyses provide evidence consistent with household-leverage restraint and reductions in average and tail default risks. Under high-house-price state, positive housing-price shocks exert stronger risk-amplifying effects, while the risk-mitigating effect of digital finance becomes more pronounced. These findings provide city-level evidence on how digital finance may strengthen financial resilience in regions undergoing rapid digital transformation.

title: Development of BASEER: a comprehensive Arabic–English process improvement platform integrating Lean Six Sigma tools with AI-powered waste classification
summary: Purpose This paper aims to address the limited success of Lean Six Sigma (LSS) initiatives in Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) contexts, where cultural and linguistic misalignment often undermines adoption. It introduces and pilots BASEER, a bilingual Arabic–English digital platform designed to embed LSS tools into public sector and service organizations while accounting for linguistic nuance and organizational culture. Design/methodology/approach Using a minimum viable product (MVP) approach, BASEER was iteratively developed and refined through workshops involving Omani Government ministries. Feedback from participants guided system enhancements, while natural language processing (NLP) models were trained and evaluated on a data set of 1,041 Arabic operational statements across eight waste categories to classify Lean wastes. Qualitative feedback, observational notes and system outputs formed the empirical base for analysis. Findings Results suggest that BASEER made improvement initiatives more inclusive by enabling broader staff participation, especially among younger and frontline employees. Compared with traditional board-and-sticker approaches, the platform facilitated faster input collection, more systematic waste classification and easier dissemination of visual analysis. Participants perceived BASEER as better aligned with local context than consultant-led interventions, though findings remain perception-based rather than quantitatively validated. Research limitations/implications As an MVP pilot, this study is limited to workshop settings in Oman and relies largely on participant feedback. Broader testing across GCC countries, the private sector and larger data sets is required to confirm generalizability. Dialectal variation in Arabic also presents ongoing challenges for NLP integration. Practical implications BASEER demonstrates that LSS tools can be localized for Arabic-speaking environments. By embedding improvement tools in culturally sensitive, bilingual formats, the platform provides a more sustainable model for government and service-sector organizations pursuing digital transformation. Social implications By enabling staff at all levels to contribute feedback in their native language, BASEER promotes more inclusive decision-making within government and service organizations. This fosters greater transparency, reduces barriers to participation and supports a shift from individual blame to systemic improvement. In the wider social context, culturally adapted quality platforms can strengthen public trust in services, enhance citizen satisfaction and reduce the dependency on external consultants whose recommendations may not reflect local realities. This study highlights how digital transformation, when culturally grounded, can advance both organizational excellence and social equity. Originality/value To the best of the author’s knowledge, this is among the first studies to integrate Arabic NLP with LSS for public-sector applications. It contributes to the Quality 4.0 literature by suggesting that digital transformation must address not only technological sophistication but also linguistic inclusivity and cultural alignment. The paper offers an early model for adapting global methodologies into locally relevant, user-friendly digital tools.

title: Endogenous Corporate Social Responsibility in a Congested Network Monopoly: Passive Versus Responsive Consumer Expectations
summary: ABSTRACT This paper examines endogenous corporate social responsibility (CSR) in a monopolistic network industry in which participation generates both network benefits and congestion. We develop a fulfilled‐expectations model and compare the firm's CSR, pricing and output decisions under passive and responsive consumer expectations. Under passive expectations, positive network externalities always sustain CSR, whereas sufficiently strong congestion may eliminate commitment when consumers' sensitivity to CSR is limited. Under responsive expectations, CSR is always strictly positive. Whenever the passive solution is interior, responsive expectations induce stronger CSR under congestion but weaker CSR when positive network benefits dominate. The profit and welfare rankings across expectation regimes similarly depend on the nature of network interactions. Nevertheless, within each regime, endogenous CSR raises monopoly profit, consumer surplus and social surplus relative to the corresponding no‐CSR benchmark whenever it is adopted. These findings remain robust when production involves increasing marginal costs. Allowing for heterogeneous expectations further shows that, under congestion, a sufficiently large share of responsive consumers can eliminate the no‐CSR outcome.

title: Sistem Pendukung Keputusan Penilaian Kesiapan UMKM Go-Digital Menggunakan Metode EDAS Berbasis Web
summary: Low levels of digital readiness and information technology literacy prevent many MSME from optimally utilizing digital platforms to support their business processes. This presents a significant challenge for accelerating digital transformation, particularly in Medan. This study aims to develop a web-based decision support system using the EDAS method to assess the level of readiness of MSME to go digital. This study employed a descriptive quantitative approach, with a sample of 15 MSME selected through a Likert-scale questionnaire. The data obtained were analyzed using the EDAS method to determine digital readiness scores based on established criteria and sub-criteria. title: Consumer Perceptions of Corporate Social Responsibility: A Decision-Analytics Perspective on Gender and Target-Group Differences
summary: Corporate social responsibility (CSR) has evolved from a voluntary corporate activity into a strategic management tool that influences organizational competitiveness, corporate reputation, and long-term sustainability. At the same time, consumers increasingly expect companies to address social and environmental challenges through responsible business practices, making consumer responses to CSR an important consideration in corporate decision-making. Although previous studies have extensively investigated CSR-related consumer behavior, relatively little attention has been paid to the simultaneous examination of gender differences and consumer segmentation based on CSR preferences. Addressing this gap, this study investigates consumer preferences toward different CSR dimensions and examines how these preferences vary across demographic groups. From a decision-analytical perspective, identifying homogeneous consumer groups according to their CSR-related attitudes can provide valuable support for corporate decision-makers in designing sustainability strategies and stakeholder communication. Accordingly, the practical objective of the study is to identify the CSR dimensions that consumers consider most important and determine how these preferences differ across demographic groups, while the methodological objective is to apply K-means clustering to identify homogeneous consumer segments based on their CSR-related preferences.

It substantiates the need to develop an AV Transformation Concept aimed at creating a digital property valuation ecosystem. Its key elements are described, including digital data, automated valuation models, machine-readable reports, risk-based quality control, and new professional appraiser competencies. title: Urban Computing Infrastructure and the Integration of Digitalisation and Green Development in Enterprises
summary: One of the main problems of the digital economy in recent years is how to achieve the combined development of digitalisation and green transformation in enterprises. Based on the data of Chinese A-share listed companies, this paper will systematically study the impact, transmission mechanism and heterogeneity of urban computing infrastructure on enterprise integration in digital and green development over time using a time-fixed-effects model. Based on the above results, it can be concluded that the urban computing infrastructure has a positive effect on enterprises' integration of digital and green development, and this effect is robust to all kinds of sensitivity tests, such as adding control variables, changing the sample period, modifying standard errors, lagging explanatory variables and including industry fixed effects. Based on the analysis of the mechanism, the computing infrastructure will reduce financing constraints, promote the integration of industry and increase real-economy industrial upgrading and enterprise innovation. Based on the test of heterogeneity, the positive effect is relatively strong for non-state-owned enterprises and in non-competitive industries. This paper provides empirical evidence on the use of computing infrastructure for digital-green development in enterprises and offers policy recommendations to help the government tackle the problem of carbon emissions from infrastructure construction by means of differentiated policies.

title: IMPLEMENTASI PRINSIP ENVIRONMENTAL, SOCIAL, AND GOVERNANCE (ESG) DAN TANGGUNG JAWAB DIREKSI DALAM KERANGKA GOOD CORPORATE GOVERNANCE: STUDI KASUS PADA PT INTICORP LOGISTICS
summary: Abstract: This study analyses the legal position of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) principles within the framework of Good Corporate Governance (GCG), examines the implementation of ESG at PT Inticorp Logistics, and assesses the legal responsibility of the Board of Directors for ESG implementation under Indonesian company law. A normative juridical method was used with statutory, conceptual, and normative case study approaches. The analysis drew on Law Number 40 of 2007 on Limited Liability Companies, Financial Services Authority Regulation Number 51/POJK.03/2017, the G20/OECD Principles of Corporate Governance (2023), the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards, and the doctrines of fiduciary duty, duty of care, duty of loyalty, and the business judgment rule, applied to the company's documents. The findings show that PT Inticorp Logistics has implemented ESG at the operational level through quality management, occupational health and safety systems, and a basic corporate governance structure. However, ESG has not been integrated into the directors' strategic policies, risk management, performance indicators, or sustainability reporting. Indonesian positive law does not explicitly require all companies to adopt ESG, so the absence of an ESG policy does not in itself constitute a breach of law. Nevertheless, ESG holds an implicit legal position as part of the directors' duty to manage the company in good faith and with due care. This study proposes a legal construction of ESG-based directors' responsibility that positions ESG integration as a concrete manifestation of fiduciary duty and duty of care. Keyword: Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG); directors' responsibility; fiduciary duty; good corporate governance; logistics company. Abstrak: Penelitian ini menganalisis kedudukan hukum prinsip Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) dalam kerangka Good Corporate Governance (GCG), mengkaji implementasi ESG pada PT Inticorp Logistics, serta menilai tanggung jawab hukum Direksi dalam penerapan ESG berdasarkan hukum perseroan Indonesia. Penelitian menggunakan metode yuridis normatif dengan pendekatan perundang-undangan, konseptual, dan studi kasus normatif. Analisis didasarkan pada Undang-Undang Nomor 40 Tahun 2007 tentang Perseroan Terbatas, POJK Nomor 51/POJK.03/2017, G20/OECD Principles of Corporate Governance (2023), IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards, serta doktrin fiduciary duty, duty of care, duty of loyalty, dan business judgment rule yang diterapkan pada dokumen perusahaan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa PT Inticorp Logistics telah menerapkan ESG pada tingkat operasional melalui sistem manajemen mutu, keselamatan dan kesehatan kerja, serta struktur dasar tata kelola perusahaan. Namun, ESG belum terintegrasi ke dalam kebijakan strategis Direksi, manajemen risiko, indikator kinerja, maupun pelaporan keberlanjutan. Hukum positif Indonesia belum secara eksplisit mewajibkan seluruh perseroan menerapkan ESG, sehingga ketiadaan kebijakan ESG tidak serta-merta merupakan pelanggaran hukum. Meskipun demikian, ESG memiliki kedudukan hukum secara implisit sebagai bagian dari kewajiban Direksi untuk mengurus perseroan dengan itikad baik dan penuh kehati-hatian. Penelitian ini menawarkan konstruksi hukum tanggung jawab Direksi berbasis ESG yang menempatkan integrasi ESG sebagai manifestasi konkret fiduciary duty dan duty of care. title: MODERATING EFFECT OF FIRM AGE ON AUDIT COMMITTEE ATTRIBUTES AND FINANCIAL REPORTING LAG OF LISTED INSURANCE FIRMS IN NIGERIA
summary: Financial reporting delays remain a significant governance concern because late financial information may lose relevance for investors, regulators and other stakeholders. This study examined the moderating effect of firm age on the relationship between audit committee independence and diligence and financial reporting lag among listed insurance firms in Nigeria. The study was anchored on Stakeholder Theory and Resource Dependency Theory. A correlational research design was adopted using secondary data from the annual reports and accounts of 12 listed insurance firms over 2016–2025, producing 120 firm-year observations. Pooled ordinary least squares (OLS), fixed-effects and random-effects panel models were estimated, while the Breusch–Pagan Lagrange Multiplier and Hausman specification tests guided model selection. Heteroskedasticity was detected and robust standard errors were therefore used for inference. The results indicate that audit committee independence has no significant relationship with financial reporting lag. Audit committee diligence has a positive and significant relationship with financial reporting lag, while firm age also has a positive and significant relationship with financial reporting lag. Firm age does not significantly moderate the independence relationship with financial reporting lag but significantly moderates audit committee diligence relationship with financial reporting lag. The study concludes that meeting frequency alone does not necessarily translate into faster reporting and that the governance effect of diligence varies with organisational age. It recommends stronger substantive audit committee oversight, early resolution of reporting bottlenecks and age-sensitive governance interventions

title: Analyzing the role of business digitization interface in the humanitarian services supply chain for community well-being
summary: Purpose This study aims to reduce the hurdles in the humanitarian services supply chain (HSSC) deliverance with digitization. This will help reduce the communication and execution gap between the participating organization, suppliers and ground-level welfare service vendors. Design/methodology/approach The hybrid Plan-Do-Check-Act–fuzzy Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution approach was adapted to strategize, address and prioritize the key strategic benefits (KSBs) of using business digitization interface (BDIs) with an interactive dashboard for data visualization and efficient monitoring. Findings The HSSCs typically depend on the availability of funds, procurement of relief materials, allocation of projects, engagement of service vendors and project execution. A unique approach was adapted to visualize the HSSC using BDIs to reduce inefficiencies in conventional tender-based welfare systems and international aid for Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 3, SDG7 and SDG11. Research limitations/implications The study reflects the use of data visualization in non-profit community development activities with the Technology–Organization–Environment–Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology approach. This replaces the old conventional methods of favored/non-transparent tender allotments. Non-profit organizations often lack access to funds to implement modern technology. However, adopting cost-effective, sustainable technology will pave the way for performance improvements and future adaptations. Practical implications The dashboard created with BDI enables ground-level implementation with direct source connectivity integrated with blockchain, Internet of Things and artificial intelligence. This implementation can be a digital twin that will bring resilience to HSSCs. Social implications Adapting BDIs for managerial activities will expedite welfare tasks. This study can guide the digitization of international humanitarian aid efforts if implemented. summary: This article presents an audit of the storage practices at the Medical Supplies Division (MSD) in Sri Lanka, evaluating their compliance with the Good Storage Practices (GSP) guidelines set by the National Medicines Regulatory Authority (NMRA). It also highlights the imperative for digital transformation and the role of international collaboration in addressing systemic challenges. The article proposes recommendations for continuous improvement to enhance the integrity of the medical supply chain in Sri Lanka.

title: Open innovation for sustainable urban transformation in Kazakhstan's monotowns: integrating digital transformation, ESG governance, and urban-territorial resilience
summary: Resource-dependent monotowns face interconnected urban sustainability challenges arising from economic concentration, environmental degradation, technological dependence, infrastructure pressures, demographic change, and institutional vulnerability. Addressing these challenges requires an integrated approach to sustainable urban transformation that combines digital innovation, environmental responsibility, social inclusion, and urban resilience. This conceptual study develops an integrative framework explaining how open innovation can connect digital transformation and ESG-oriented urban governance to strengthen the resilience and sustainability of Kazakhstan's monotowns. Using a qualitative conceptual approach, the study synthesizes academic literature, international policy documents, and Kazakhstan's national strategic documents through thematic analysis to identify seven interrelated themes and inform the proposed framework. The present study is intentionally theory-building and conceptual and does not claim empirical validation of the proposed relationships. Drawing on Regional Resilience Theory, Evolutionary Economic Geography, Open Innovation Theory, the Quadruple Helix Model, and sustainability governance, the framework conceptualizes monotowns as resource-dependent urban-regional systems in which government, industry, universities, and communities jointly shape sustainable transformation. The framework identifies digital infrastructure, smart technologies, data-enabled governance, knowledge exchange, collaborative innovation, institutional adaptability, human-capital development, and ESG-oriented governance as interconnected mechanisms supporting sustainable urban infrastructure, environmental resource management, economic diversification, social inclusion, and resilient urban development. Open innovation is positioned as the bridging mechanism through which digital and sustainability transitions can be coordinated across urban stakeholders. The study contributes to sustainable cities research by integrating innovation ecosystems, digital transformation, ESG-oriented urban governance, and urban-territorial resilience within a place-sensitive framework. The framework also provides policy directions to advance SDG 11 and support inclusive, environmentally responsible, technologically enabled, and resilient transformation of resource-dependent monotowns.

title: Blockchain integration in maritime logistics: identifying key factors and implementation roadmap
summary: This study identifies 35 critical drivers of blockchain adoption in maritime logistics and develops a structured 10-level implementation roadmap. The factors are classified across nine dimensions and modelled using Total Interpretive Structural Modelling, with MICMAC analysis determining their driving and dependence powers. The resulting hierarchy proposes a sequential transition system from technological infrastructure to managerial, stakeholder, and regulatory integration. The roadmap is validated through real-world maritime blockchain cases, including both successful implementations and a failure-based diagnostic analysis. The findings translate fragmented theoretical insights into an operational, stage-based framework, providing practical guidance for blockchain-driven digital transformation in maritime logistics.

title: Market Growth Strategies of Clothing Brands Driven by Digital Marketing: A Case Study of UNIQLO
summary: Focusing on how digital marketing drives market growth of clothing brands, this paper takes the fast fashion brand UNIQLO as a case study. It adopts a case study, literature review, and secondary data analysis to map out the brand's digital marketing layout and specific tactics, and unpacks the underlying mechanisms based on the analytical framework of "digital marketing strategy - consumer behavior mediation - market growth outcome". The study finds that digital marketing facilitates multi-dimensional brand growth through three paths: traffic expansion, conversion efficiency improvement, and brand value enhancement. UNIQLO has built a steady growth loop through omni-channel integration, scene-based content marketing, a digital membership system, and cross-channel synergy, which effectively boosts its market performance. However, multiple challenges remain in its digital practice, including content homogenization, insufficient depth of private domain operation, and slow adoption of live-streaming commerce. These drawbacks limit its further growth potential in the Chinese market. The findings of this paper provide practical references for the digital transformation and online marketing strategy optimization of domestic clothing brands.

title: The Ontology of Blocking Law: From Regulatory History to Conceptual Return
summary: Against the background of the expansion of extraterritorial jurisdiction, this paper points out that blocking law should not be reduced solely to the binary narrative of "extraterritorial foreign legislation infringing national interests – domestic defense of national interests." Its institutional evolution has progressed from blocking evidence discovery and the enforcement of foreign judgments in the competition-law context to a comprehensive framework under restrictive measures law encompassing "prohibition of compliance – shielding against foreign judgments – damages relief – reporting and exemption." At the level of international law, extraterritorial legislation merely extends the scope of application of the norm and does not necessarily project state power; the legitimacy of blocking law is therefore better explained as the use of domestic private international law tools to uphold reasonable nexus, international comity, and the avoidance of inconsistent obligations. At the level of domestic law, restrictive measures law pierces foreign property rights, corporate governance, and freedom of contract by relying on financial infrastructure and compliance deterrence; blocking law, by amending choice-of-law references, restricting the recognition and enforcement of foreign judgments, and supplementing these with prohibition of compliance and civil relief, achieves a "corrective realignment" of the domestic private-law order. Blocking law is thus an instrument combining unilateral countermeasure and order-repair: it denies the effect of foreign public law within the forum state, while returning private-law relations to domestic law.

title: Leasing as a Corporate Financing Strategy from a Management Accounting Perspective: A Literature Review Following the Implementation of PSAK 73 (PSAK 116)
summary: The increasing demand for productive assets has encouraged companies to adopt leasing as an alternative financing strategy that supports business expansion without requiring substantial initial capital investment. The implementation of PSAK 73, which was renumbered as PSAK 116 effective January 1, 2024, has transformed lease accounting by requiring the recognition of right-of-use assets and lease liabilities in the statement of financial position, thereby affecting liquidity, capital structure, and corporate financial performance. This study aims to analyze leasing as a corporate financing strategy from a management accounting perspective using a literature review approach. The data were obtained from accounting standards, academic books, and national and international scholarly publications published between 2020 and 2025. The analysis was conducted through the identification, classification, synthesis, and interpretation of literature discussing lease-versus-buy analysis, Net Present Value (NPV), Net Advantage to Leasing (NAL), cash flow analysis, capital structure, and the implications of PSAK 116 implementation. The findings indicate that leasing enhances financing flexibility, maintains liquidity, and optimizes the allocation of corporate financial resources. However, the recognition of lease liabilities under PSAK 116 may increase leverage and influence the interpretation of profitability ratios. This study concludes that leasing is a strategic financing instrument that supports financial planning, investment decision-making, and sustainable corporate financial risk management.

title: INSTITUTIONAL CONSTRAINTS ON THE DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION OF UKRAINIAN AGRICULTURAL SECTOR
summary: This study investigates the theoretical and methodological foundations and tools of digital transformation in Ukraineʼs agricultural sector and develops scientific and methodological approaches to establishing a system of indicators for assessing agricultural digital maturity in the context of sustainable development and European integration. The hypothesis is put forward that the effectiveness of digital transformation is deter­mined not so much by the level of implementation of individual digital technologies as by the coherence of organisational, economic, techno­logical, and institutional tools that ensure their integration into the agricultural sector manage­ment system. The hypothesis was tested through the systematisation of scientific approaches to the digitalisation of agricultural production, compa­rative and structural-functional analysis, asses­sment of the relationships between digitali­sation indicators, innovation potential, and sustainable development, and an examination of official statistical data, European Commission materials, and international indices, including the Global Innovation Index and the Digital Economy and Society Index. It was established that the digital transformation of the agricultural sector is a comprehensive process encompassing the use of precision agriculture technologies, sensor and satellite monitoring, the Internet of Things, Big Data, artificial intelligence, geographic informa­tion systems, unmanned technologies, and digital management platforms. Indicators for assessing digital transformation were systematised into technological, economic, environmental, social, and institutional blocks, enabling a compre­hensive assessment of the level of digital maturity of the agricultural sector and the effectiveness of digital solutions implementation. Technological heterogeneity of the agricultural sector was identified, manifested in a significant gap between digitally mature large enterprises and small and medium-sized producers with limited access to digital infrastructure, financial resources, and modern digital competencies. Methods and tools for digital transformation were systematised according to organisational, economic, techno­logical, and institutional criteria. The feasibility of their integrated application was substantiated to ensure the relationship between digital modernisation and increased efficiency of agri­cul­tural production. The proposed approach can be used to improve state digitalisation policy, substantiate priorities for supporting agricultural enterprises, and monitor the effectiveness of digital transformation in Ukraineʼs agricultural sector.

title: The Influence of Islamic Capital Market Education and Literacy on Students’ Investment Activity in Digital Sharia Investment Platforms
summary: Despite the growing number of students with sharia investment accounts, active participation in digital Islamic investment platforms remains limited indicating a gap between financial education and actual investment behavior. This study examines the influence of Islamic capital market education and literacy on students’ investment activity on digital sharia platforms. Using a quantitative explanatory approach, data were collected from 95 students in the fifth and seventh semesters of the Faculty of Islamic Economics and Business (FEBI) at UIN North Sumatra, selected through purposive sampling. Data were analyzed using multiple linear regression with SPSS version 27. The results show that Islamic capital market education has a positive but statistically non-significant effect on investment activity (β = 0.415; t = 1.726; Sig = 0.088). In contrast, Islamic capital market literacy has a positive and significant effect (β = 0.717; t = 3.274; Sig = 0.001), making it the most dominant predictor (standardized β = 0.463). Simultaneously, both variables significantly explain 46.5% of the variation in investment activity (F = 39.997; Sig= 0.000). These findings suggest that improving applied literacy not merely theoretical education is essential to stimulate active investment behavior, with practical implications for curriculum design, investment gallery programs, and Islamic fintech platform development targeting university students..

title: Corporate Social Responsibility, Legitimacy, and Rhetorical Responses to Social Activism: Evidence From the Black Lives Matter Movement
summary: ABSTRACT This study investigates how large corporations rhetorically respond to social activism and how such responses are used to construct and manage corporate legitimacy. Using the Black Lives Matter (BLM) movement as an empirical context, the study examines how corporate social responsibility (CSR) communication attempts to shape organizational discourse and the development of diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) policies. Drawing on qualitative analyses of multi‐source data from CSR disclosures, annual reports, executive communications, and media outputs of 50 firms from the Fortune 500 , the study employs systematic content and thematic analyses to examine how organizations construct, articulate, and legitimize their responses to social activism. The findings demonstrate that corporations strategically attempt to deploy logos, ethos, and pathos to construct cognitive, pragmatic, and moral legitimacy, with rhetorical patterns varying across industries and communication platforms. Overall, the study advances CSR and business ethics scholarship by theorizing corporate rhetoric as a central mechanism through which firms navigate legitimacy under conditions of heightened social scrutiny.

title: Digitalization, Techno-Stressor, and Digital Readiness: Their Effects on Job Stress and MSMEs’ Performance
summary: Digitalization in the Society 4.0 era has accelerated digital technology adoption among MSMEs, generating both operational benefits and technology-related psychological pressures. This study examines the effects of digitalization on job stress and digital performance among MSMEs in Yogyakarta, with techno-stressor as a mediator and digital readiness as a moderator. Survey data from 171 MSME owners and managers were analyzed using PLS-SEM with SmartPLS 4.1. Digitalization did not significantly affect job stress (b = 0.124, p = 0.180) or techno-stressor (b = −0.150, p = 0.107). Techno-stressor was positively associated with job stress (b = 0.670, p < 0.001), but did not mediate the digitalization–job stress relationship (b = −0.100, p = 0.117). Digital readiness did not significantly moderate the digitalization–techno-stressor relationship (b = 0.095, p = 0.070) or the digitalization–job stress relationship (b = 0.032, p = 0.480). Job stress was not associated with digital performance (b = −0.083, p = 0.093), whereas digital readiness was positively associated with digital performance (b = 0.709, p < 0.001). The findings highlight the importance of digital readiness as a resource associated with MSME digital performance and the need to manage technology-related pressure during digital transformation.

title: Digital Governance and Sustainable Performance in Romanian Public Hospitals: A Serial Mediation Model of Digital Capability, Supply Chain Visibility, and Resilience
summary: Public hospitals need supply chains that keep working under disruption, yet little is known about how digital governance relates to that outcome. This study examines a serial mediation model linking digital governance, digital capability, supply chain visibility, supply chain resilience, and sustainable performance (respondents’ perception). We surveyed 200 managers, pharmacists, procurement officers, logistics staff, financial controllers, IT specialists, and quality or risk officers from 50 Romanian public hospitals (four per hospital) in 2026. Paths were estimated by ordinary least squares on standardized composite scores, first as separate regressions and then as a recursive system, with hospital-clustered standard errors and cluster bootstrap intervals. In the recursive model, governance was related to capability (β = 0.76), capability to visibility (β = 0.64), visibility to resilience (β = 0.42), and resilience to sustainable performance (β = 0.58), all p < 0.001. The complete serial indirect association was 0.12 (95% CI [0.06, 0.18]), about 57% of the product of separate regressions, and it was smaller within hospitals (0.04), where governance varies little (ICC = 0.73). Convergent validity of visibility, resilience, and sustainable performance was weak. Under a cross-rater specification, the serial association was null, and the direct association of governance with sustainable performance changed sign, so the indirect result is not robust to the source of the ratings. The design is cross-sectional and relies on self-reports, so all results are statistical associations and do not establish causal mediation.

title: Beyond compliance: how voluntary environmental certification drives corporate green innovation in China?
summary: Green manufacturing acts as a core driver for advancing the low-carbon transition of development patterns and fostering emerging industrial growth. Drawing on Porter’s hypothesis, this study exploits the Green Factory Certification (GFC) pilot legislation as an external shock to assess its impact on green technology innovation, employing a multi-period propensity score matching difference-in-differences (PSM-DID) approach. Using a sample of Chinese A-share listed firms spanning 2010 to 2023, this study confirms that the GFC strongly promotes corporate green innovation. The paths of influence include increasing media coverage, attracting green investors, and raising managerial environmental awareness. The above finding still holds after multiple rigorous reliability checks. Heterogeneity analysis reveals that policy effects are especially noticeable in State-Owned Enterprises (SOEs), capital-intensive firms, high-tech companies, politically connected entities, and enterprises with non-traditional industrial foundations. Interestingly, while GFC helps enhance corporate value, it has negative spillover effects at the industry level. The study’s conclusions demonstrate how voluntary environmental regulations encourage corporate green innovation, which helps to increase the adoption of sustainable manufacturing practices.

title: The Effect of Perceived Usefulness of the Tring Application and Digital Service Quality on Customer Loyalty through Customer Satisfaction at PT Pegadaian, Mamuju Branch
summary: Digital transformation in the financial services sector has encouraged PT Pegadaian to develop the TRING application as a digital service platform to enhance customer satisfaction and loyalty. This study aims to analyze the effects of perceived usefulness of the TRING application and digital service quality on customer loyalty through customer satisfaction at PT Pegadaian, Mamuju Branch. This study employed a quantitative approach using a survey of 100 respondents who use the TRING application. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with the assistance of SmartPLS software. The results indicate that: (1) perceived usefulness of the TRING application has a positive and significant effect on customer satisfaction; (2) digital service quality has a positive and significant effect on customer satisfaction; (3) perceived usefulness of the TRING application has a positive but insignificant effect on customer loyalty; (4) digital service quality has a positive and significant effect on customer loyalty; (5) customer satisfaction has a positive but insignificant effect on customer loyalty; (6) perceived usefulness of the TRING application does not have a significant effect on customer loyalty through customer satisfaction; and (7) digital service quality does not have a significant effect on customer loyalty through customer satisfaction. The findings indicate that digital service quality is the most dominant factor in enhancing the loyalty of TRING application users, while customer satisfaction does not yet function as a mediating variable in the research model. Therefore, PT Pegadaian should prioritize improving digital service quality, particularly in terms of system reliability, security, ease of use, and service responsiveness, to strengthen customer loyalty.

title: Research trends in supply chain management in the construction industry: a systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis
summary: Supply chain management (SCM) has become a strategic priority in construction, where project delivery depends on coordinating fragmented actors, material flows, and information under uncertainty. Despite growing scholarly attention, research remains dispersed across sustainability, digitalisation, risk governance, and stakeholder coordination, thereby limiting the development of cumulative knowledge. To address this fragmentation, this study integrates a PRISMA 2020-guided systematic literature review with bibliometric analysis to examine the intellectual structure, thematic evolution, and future directions of construction SCM. A total of 143 studies (2001–2024) were identified from Web of Science, Scopus, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar, and analysed using descriptive techniques, thematic synthesis, and bibliographic coupling in VOSviewer. The findings reveal four interrelated domains: sustainable construction SCM, strategic management and risk mitigation, digital transformation, and supplier and stakeholder management. This review provides an integrated evidence base that clarifies field fragmentation and identifies priorities for future research and practice.

title: VALUE RELEVANCE OF ACCOUNTING INFORMATION AND MARKET PRICE PER SHARE: EVIDENCE FROM LISTED CONGLOMERATES IN NIGERIA
summary: This study examines the value relevance of accounting information and the market value of listed Nigerian conglomerates over the period 2021–2025. The study is motivated by the continuing debate on the usefulness of accounting information in explaining market valuation, particularly within emerging capital markets where investors operate under varying levels of information efficiency. The study adopts an ex-post facto research design and uses secondary data extracted from the audited annual reports and financial statements of listed Nigerian conglomerates. Market value per share (MPS) serves as the dependent variable, while earnings per share (EPS) and book value per share (BVPS) constitute the explanatory variables. The study is anchored on Ohlson’s (1995) valuation framework and employs random effects panel regression techniques, as the appropriate estimator. The findings indicate that earnings per share and book value per share have positive and statistically significant relationships with market value per share, suggesting that investors incorporate both profitability and net asset information into their valuation decisions. The study concludes that accounting information remains value relevant among listed Nigerian conglomerates. It therefore recommends that management of listed conglomerates should strengthen the quality, transparency, accuracy, and timeliness of financial reporting, particularly the disclosure of earnings and shareholders’ equity information, to enhance investor confidence and support informed investment decisions

summary: This study describes the implementation of the Village Financial System (SISKEUDES) and explores how human resource competence and digital literacy support accountability and transparency in financial management in Negeri Kailolo. A descriptive qualitative approach was used, and the study was conducted from March to April 2026. Ten informants were purposively selected from the village government, SISKEUDES operator, Village Consultative Body (BPD), and community representatives. Data were collected through interviews, observation, and documentation, then analyzed through data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing. The findings indicate that SISKEUDES supports administrative organization, data entry and storage, and financial reporting. These benefits are associated with task allocation, work experience, and staff training, although network limitations and the need for further capacity building remain. For the public, budget information is available through information boards, but community awareness and access to financial information vary. The study concludes that a gap remains between the digitization of internal administration and substantive transparency to the community. title: L'impact de la digitalisation RH sur la performance organisationnelle : Etude empirique auprès des PME marocaines
summary: Dans un contexte marqué par l'accélération de la transformation digitale, les petites et moyennes entreprises (PME) sont confrontées à la nécessité d'intégrer les technologies numériques afin d'améliorer leur compétitivité et leur performance organisationnelle. La fonction ressources humaines (RH) apparaît aujourd'hui comme l'un des principaux domaines concernés par cette mutation, à travers l'automatisation des processus, l'intégration des systèmes d'information RH et le développement des outils collaboratifs. Si la relation entre digitalisation RH et performance organisationnelle a été largement documentée dans des contextes européens et nord-américains, peu de travaux empiriques ont mobilisé des données primaires collectées auprès de PME marocaines pour l'examiner ; cet article vise précisément à combler ce déficit empirique et contextuel en analysant les perceptions d'acteurs RH marocains. L'étude repose sur une approche quantitative descriptive menée auprès de 85 répondants issus de PME opérant dans différents secteurs d'activité. Les données ont été collectées à l'aide d'un questionnaire structuré puis analysées à travers des statistiques descriptives. Les résultats montrent que la digitalisation RH est perçue par les répondants comme associée à une amélioration de la performance opérationnelle (81 %), décisionnelle (83 %) et humaine (86 %) des entreprises. L'automatisation des processus RH, l'utilisation des outils digitaux et l'acceptation des technologies par les collaborateurs apparaissent comme des leviers majeurs d'efficacité organisationnelle perçue. Toutefois, plusieurs freins persistent, notamment les contraintes financières, le manque de compétences numériques et la résistance au changement. L'étude met ainsi en évidence le rôle stratégique de la digitalisation RH dans le développement des PME et souligne la nécessité d'un accompagnement organisationnel et humain pour assurer le succès de la transformation digitale. Mots-clés : Digitalisation RH, performance organisationnelle, PME, SIRH, transformation digitale, Maroc. Abstract In a context marked by the acceleration of digital transformation, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) are increasingly required to integrate digital technologies in order to enhance their competitiveness and organizational performance. Human resource management (HRM) has emerged as one of the key areas affected by this transformation through process automation, the integration of Human Resource Information Systems (HRIS), and the development of collaborative digital tools. While the relationship between HR digitalization and organizational performance has been extensively documented in European and North American settings, few empirical studies have drawn on primary data collected from Moroccan SMEs to examine it; this article seeks to address this empirical and contextual gap by analyzing the perceptions of Moroccan HR actors. The study is based on a descriptive quantitative approach conducted among 85 respondents from SMEs operating in various sectors. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire and analyzed using descriptive statistics. The findings reveal that HR digitalization is perceived by respondents as being associated with improvements in operational (81%), decision-making (83%) and human (86%) performance within organizations. The automation of HR processes, the use of digital tools, and employees' acceptance of technology appear to be major perceived drivers of organizational efficiency. However, several challenges remain, including financial constraints, the lack of digital skills, and resistance to change. The study highlights the strategic role of HR digitalization in SME development and emphasizes the need for organizational and human support to ensure the success of digital transformation. Keywords: HR digitalization, organizational performance, SMEs, HRIS, digital transformation, Morocco.

title: Navigating digital disruptions: a supply chain cyber risk and resilience framework
summary: Purpose This study aims to develop an emergent supply chain cyber risk and resilience (SCCRR) framework, grounded in supply chain network theory (SCNT), to identify and prioritise critical cyber supply chain risks and critical resilience-enabling factors. Design/methodology/approach A multiple-case study methodology was adopted across four organisations operating in the food, pharmaceutical and logistics sectors. The framework integrates insights from extant literature and generative AI-assisted exploratory analysis. Qualitative data were analysed using template analysis, while quantitative prioritisation used multi-criteria decision-making techniques. Cross-case analysis enhanced analytical robustness and generalisability. Findings The results identify key strategies for strengthening SCCRR adoption, including integrating cybersecurity practices into supply chain operations, enhancing cross-sector collaboration for threat intelligence sharing and deploying advanced monitoring systems to detect vulnerabilities. The findings further reveal that organisations with lower levels of SCCRR integration exhibit weaker adaptive capacity, highlighting areas where targeted investments, such as vendor audit protocols, crisis management training, and decentralised security architectures, deliver the most significant network-wide benefits. Research limitations/implications The study provides managers with actionable, decision-support insights to prioritise cyber resilience investments across supply networks. The framework supports evidence-based decision-making by linking cyber risks, resilience capabilities and strategic interventions. Originality/value This research advances SCNT-based resilience theory by operationalising cyber risk and resilience through an empirically grounded, decision-oriented framework. It contributes to practice-relevant supply chain research by translating theory-driven network analysis into implementable managerial tools within real-world organisational contexts.

title: Institutional Configuration and Governance Capacity for E-Government Development in Asia–Pacific Economies
summary: This study examines how institutional structure and coordination capacity shape e-government development in Asia–Pacific economies. Using panel data for 12 countries from 2003 to 2024 and United Nations E-Government Development Index data, the study estimates fixed-effects, random-effects, and high-dimensional fixed-effects models. The results show that institutional design conditions the role of governance quality rather than determining it uniformly. In the high-dimensional fixed-effects specification, the interaction between hybrid governance structures and government effectiveness is positive and statistically significant, indicating larger EGDI gains from improved administrative effectiveness under hybrid arrangements. The interaction between hybrid structures and regulatory quality is also positive and significant. By contrast, centralized structures have a negative direct association with EGDI in fixed-effects models, although their interaction with high governance quality becomes positive in the high-dimensional fixed-effects specification. These findings suggest that digital transformation depends on the alignment between institutional structure and governance capacity. Policy implications emphasize combining strategic central direction with decentralized flexibility, strengthening administrative coordination, and investing in human capital.

title: Zero dividend policy and corporate governance: integrative framework
summary: Purpose: This study develops an integrative theoretical framework explaining why firms deliberately adopt and sustain zero dividend policies. While dividend payout behaviour has been widely examined, limited attention has been given to firms that consistently refrain from distributing cash dividends. This paper addresses this gap by synthesising governance, strategic, and behavioural mechanisms underlying zero dividend decisions, with particular relevance to European listed companies Design/methodology/approach: This conceptual study is based on an integrative literature review supported by bibliometric mapping. Publications indexed in Scopus and Web of Science were analysed to identify dominant research streams and thematic structures in dividend policy research. Insights from agency theory, signalling theory, corporate governance theory, and investor behaviour are combined to develop a multidimensional conceptual framework. Findings: Zero dividend policy may function as a governance mechanism, a potential source of agency conflict, and a strategic market signal. Its implications depend on governance quality, ownership structure, and investor sophistication. Sustained non-payment of dividends should be interpreted as a deliberate managerial strategy influenced by institutional and market conditions, particularly within European corporate environments. Limitations and further research: The review is limited to English language publications and selected high quality journals, which may exclude relevant contributions from other contexts. Future empirical studies should test the proposed framework across European institutional settings and examine managerial motivations using primary data Practical implications: The proposed framework provides guidance for investors, regulators and corporate decision makers in evaluating the governance implications and market interpretation of sustained zero dividend strategies. Originality/value: The study conceptualises zero dividend policy as a strategic corporate governance phenomenon rather than merely a residual financial outcome and establishes a foundation for subsequent empirical investigation. title: Diffusion and Dissemination of Innovation in The Context of Distance Higher Education in Indonesia
summary: This study evaluates the process of innovation diffusion and explores the characteristics of innovation dissemination patterns in distance higher education (PTJJ) in Indonesia, using the MyUT application at Universitas Terbuka (UT) as a case study. This digital innovation was designed to integrate student academic services online within a single platform. The research used an exploratory qualitative case study approach, drawing on in-depth interviews, field observations, and documentation involving UT staff, regional UT managers, and students from various regions. The analysis shows that MyUT's diffusion follows Rogers’ five-stage model (knowledge, persuasion, decision, implementation, and confirmation), mediated by geographical context, digital literacy, and organizational culture. Innovation disseminates not only through formal structural channels from the central office to regional units but is also reinforced by horizontal networks among users, including opinion leaders within student and tutor communities. The study finds that the successful adoption of MyUT depends on a combination of hierarchical and participatory approaches, along with scaffolding that supports the digital transition. These findings imply that innovation diffusion in distance higher education requires adaptive communication strategies, interactive support, and a stronger organizational culture open to digital transformation. title: MODERATING EFFECT OF AUDIT FIRM TYPE ON THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN BOARD ATTRIBUTES AND ESG DISCLOSURES
summary: The growing emphasis on sustainability has heightened the importance of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) disclosures among listed firms, particularly in emerging economies such as Nigeria. This study examines the effects of board composition, board gender diversity, and CSR/sustainability committees on ESG disclosures among 55 non-financial firms listed on the Nigerian Exchange (NGX) from 2014 to 2025, while investigating the moderating role of audit firm type. Anchored on Legitimacy Theory, the study adopts a positivist philosophy and ex post facto research design, with Panel Corrected Standard Error (PCSE) regression employed for data analysis. The findings reveal that board gender diversity and CSR/sustainability committees have positive and significant effects on ESG disclosures, whereas board composition has a positive but insignificant effect. The results further show that audit firm type significantly strengthens the relationships between board attributes and ESG disclosures, indicating that firms audited by Big Four audit firms tend to provide more credible and comprehensive sustainability information. The study concludes that effective ESG disclosure requires a combination of strong internal governance mechanisms and high-quality external auditing. It recommends greater gender diversity on corporate boards, the establishment and effective functioning of board-level CSR/sustainability committees, and enhanced audit quality to improve ESG reporting, accountability, and corporate transparency among listed firms in Nigeria.

title: Building Cyber Resilient IT Service Organizations Through Digital Leadership and Employee Cybersecurity Capability
summary: The rapid advancement of digital transformation has significantly enhanced organizational efficiency while simultaneously increasing exposure to sophisticated cyber threats that may compromise business continuity, stakeholder trust, and long-term organizational sustainability. These challenges require IT service organizations to strengthen cyber resilience by integrating effective digital leadership with employee cybersecurity capability, thereby fostering a secure, innovative, and sustainable digital ecosystem. This study aims to examine the influence of digital leadership on employee cybersecurity capability and its subsequent impact on organizational cyber resilience. A quantitative research approach was employed using a survey of employees working in IT service organizations, and the proposed research model was analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings indicate that digital leadership positively and significantly enhances employee cybersecurity capability, which in turn plays a crucial role in strengthening organizational cyber resilience. Furthermore, employee cybersecurity capability acts as a significant mediating mechanism between digital leadership and cyber resilience, enabling organizations to anticipate, detect, respond to, and recover more effectively from evolving cyber threats. These findings demonstrate that adaptive digital leadership combined with continuous investment in employees' cybersecurity competencies constitutes a critical organizational capability for maintaining resilient digital operations and sustaining long-term organizational performance. This study contributes to the growing literature on digital leadership and cyber resilience while providing strategic insights for IT service organizations seeking to establish a sustainable cybersecurity culture that supports resilient digital infrastructure and inclusive technological innovation.

title: Web-Based CRM System with Non-Preemptive SJF Scheduling and WhatsApp Notifications for Clothing Alteration MSMEs
summary: Digital transformation has become a key strategy for enhancing operational efficiency and service quality in Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs). However, clothing alteration MSMEs continue to face challenges in customer management, order recording, and service queue management due to the absence of an integrated system. This study develops a web-based Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system that integrates Non-Preemptive Shortest Job First (SJF) scheduling with automated WhatsApp notifications. The research employs the Research and Development (R&D) method using the Waterfall System Development Life Cycle (SDLC) model, with data collected through observations, interviews, and a literature review. The proposed system integrates customer, order, and SJF-based queue management with real-time service notifications. Evaluation results indicate that the proposed SJF scheduling method reduced the Average Waiting Time (AWT) from 9.8 hours to 4.0 hours and the Average Turnaround Time (ATT) from 13.4 hours to 7.6 hours compared with the First Come First Served (FCFS) method. In addition, the system achieved a 90% WhatsApp notification delivery success rate and an 84.22% User Acceptance Testing (UAT) score, indicating that it enhances service quality, strengthens customer communication, and improves service queue management for clothing alteration MSMEs.

title: Product Innovation and SME Performance: The Roles of Strategic Orientations and IT Utilization in Batik SMEs
summary: This study explores how small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in traditional cultural sectors—like Trusmi's batik industry—balance cultural preservation with market adaptation and digital transformation. Prior research often views market orientation, entrepreneurial orientation, and IT utilization as direct performance drivers, but their mechanisms—especially in culturally rooted industries—remain understudied. The research highlights product innovation as a critical intermediary, linking these three capabilities to performance. It examines whether IT enhances performance directly or indirectly by fostering innovation. A quantitative survey of 51 batik SMEs in Trusmi, analyzed using PLS-SEM (SmartPLS 4.0), finds that market orientation, entrepreneurial orientation, and IT utilization significantly boost product innovation, which in turn improves performance. Key findings include IT's negative direct effect on performance but a positive indirect effect through innovation, indicating inconsistent mediation. Theoretically, this extends the Resource-Based View and Dynamic Capabilities Perspective, showing IT's value lies in driving innovation. Practically, batik SMEs should integrate IT into customer value creation rather than adopting it passively. Ultimately, performance depends on SMEs' ability to convert resources—including IT—into innovations that align with market demands. The study emphasizes innovation'​s role as a bridge between capabilities and sustained success in culturally significant industries.

title: The Effect Of Digital Literacy On Digital Readiness Among Tirtonadi Terminal Employees: The Mediating Role Of Digital Competence
summary: This study examines the effect of digital literacy on digital readiness among employees of Tirtonadi Terminal, Surakarta, and tests digital competence as a mediating mechanism. A quantitative explanatory design was used with 120 employees selected from a population of 172 through simple random sampling. Data were collected using a five-point Likert questionnaire covering digital literacy, digital competence, and digital readiness, and were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4. The measurement model met convergent validity, discriminant validity, and reliability criteria. Digital literacy significantly increased digital competence (β = 0.711; t = 12.302; p < 0.001) and digital readiness (β = 0.740; t = 14.262; p < 0.001), while digital competence significantly improved digital readiness (β = 0.485; t = 6.070; p < 0.001). The indirect effect was also significant (β = 0.345; t = 4.931; p < 0.001), indicating partial mediation. The findings show that literacy provides the cognitive and technical foundation for digital adaptation, while competence converts that foundation into work-related capability. Public transport organizations should therefore combine digital-literacy development with practical competence training to strengthen employee readiness for continuing digital transformation
