title: Transforming Industry 4.0 technologies into sustainable business performance through technology implementation and government policy support
summary: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) increasingly adopt Industry 4.0 technologies to improve sustainability, yet firms often struggle to translate these technological investments into meaningful performance outcomes. This study examines how Industry 4.0 technologies, including big data (BiD), the Internet of Things (IoT), and cyber-physical systems (CPS), contribute to sustainable business performance (SBP) by considering the mediating role of technology implementation and the moderating role of government policy. Using a time-lagged survey design, data were collected from 388 SMEs in Pakistan and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). The findings demonstrate that BiD, IoT, and CPS positively influence SBP. Technology implementation significantly mediates the relationships between Industry 4.0 technologies and SBP. Furthermore, government policy strengthens the relationships of BiD and CPS with SBP, while its moderating effect on IoT is insignificant. This study contributes to the industry 4.0 and sustainability literature by demonstrating that digital technologies function as strategic resources whose value depends on implementation capabilities and targeted support. The findings provide practical implications for SME managers and policymakers by emphasizing capability development, digital infrastructure, and technology-specific policy interventions to achieve sustainable digital transformation.

title: Maritime Corridor Readiness Under Chokepoint Disruption: A Distributionally Robust Decision Model for Eastern Mediterranean Supply Chains
summary: Maritime chokepoint exposure can be quantified, but supply-chain risk management still requires an ex ante decision about which alternatives to keep ready. The objective is to identify and evaluate an ex ante corridor-readiness portfolio before the disruption state is known, while accounting for shared regional capacity, distributional ambiguity, and tail risk. This study models the Eastern Mediterranean as an interconnected maritime-logistics system comprising five countries, five sectors, five corridors, and six empirically calibrated disruption states. A two-stage distributionally robust decision model couples pre-disruption corridor readiness with post-disruption flow recourse under shared regional capacities, Wasserstein ambiguity, and CVaR tail-risk pricing. Relative to the inferred status quo, the optimized portfolio reduces the composite USD-equivalent objective by USD 241.623 billion, equivalent to 22.6% of the model’s average annual trade-account base under the maintained normalization. This is a calibrated benchmark-distance-to-base ratio, not a realized saving. The optimized portfolio concentrates readiness and improves aggregate performance, yet it performs USD 14.465 billion worse in the Turkish Straits disruption state. Doubling and renormalizing that state’s policy weight shifts the portfolio away from the Turkish Straits and reverses the state-specific loss. The contribution is a transparent decision-analytics framework that places system boundaries, infrastructure interdependencies, advance preparedness, recourse, and residual vulnerability in one auditable supply-chain risk model.

title: Artificial Intelligence, ESG Disclosure Quality, and Corporate Sustainability Performance in Islamic Banking: The Role of Sharia Governance
summary: This study examines the relationships among Artificial Intelligence (AI), ESG Disclosure Quality (ESGDQ), Greenwashing, and Corporate Sustainability Performance (CSP), and investigates the moderating role of Sharia Governance in Islamic banking. The study employs a quantitative explanatory design using panel data from Islamic commercial banks in Indonesia and Malaysia during the 2021–2025 period. The study collected data from annual reports, sustainability reports, corporate governance reports, official corporate websites, and other publicly available disclosures through structured content analysis and disclosure-based indices. The hypotheses were tested using a fixed-effects panel regression model. The findings indicate that disclosed AI capability and implementation are positively associated with ESG Disclosure Quality, while AI is not significantly associated with Greenwashing. ESG Disclosure Quality is positively associated with Corporate Sustainability Performance, whereas Greenwashing is not significantly associated with sustainability performance. Sharia Governance strengthens the positive relationship between AI and ESG Disclosure Quality but does not significantly moderate the relationship between AI and Greenwashing. These findings highlight the importance of integrating technological capabilities with Sharia Governance to support more credible, transparent, and responsible sustainability reporting practices in Islamic banking.

title: Managing The Organizational Climate in The Digital Era for Teachers at SMP Negeri 4 Pakem and SMP Binajaya Banguntapan
summary: This study aimed to analyze organizational climate management in the digital era for teachers at SMP Negeri 4 Pakem and SMP Bina Jaya Banguntapan and to identify the supporting and inhibiting factors affecting its implementation. The study employed a qualitative approach using a case study design and was conducted at two schools with distinct organizational climate characteristics. The participants included the school principals and ten teachers, comprising five teachers from SMP Negeri 4 Pakem and five teachers from SMP Bina Jaya Banguntapan. The study focused on teachers' attitudes and behaviors in their interactions with school principals and colleagues. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, structured observations using observation sheets, and document analysis. The trustworthiness of the data was assessed based on credibility, transferability, dependability, and confirmability, supported by methodological, source, and temporal triangulation. Data were analyzed using the Miles and Huberman interactive model. The findings indicated that organizational climate management in the digital era was implemented through five management functions: planning, organizing, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation. Supporting factors included the enhancement of teachers' digital competencies through training and professional learning communities, principals' transformational leadership, and school policies supporting the provision of cloud-based databases, a basic web-based management information system (MIS), and digital communication platforms. The identified barriers included limited digital literacy among teachers at SMP Bina Jaya Banguntapan, inadequate technological infrastructure, and difficulties adapting to changes in the organizational climate associated with digital transformation.

title: Profitability, Listing Age, Auditor Reputation, and Internet Financial Reporting in Indonesian Energy Companies
summary: This study examines the relationship between profitability, listing age, auditor reputation, and Internet Financial Reporting (IFR) among energy companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during 2021–2025. Secondary data were collected from financial statements and corporate websites. Purposive sampling yielded 33 companies and 165 firm-year observations. After removing 16 outliers and one observation due to the Cochrane-Orcutt correction, 148 observations were analyzed using multiple linear regression in SPSS version 24. IFR was measured using content, timeliness, technology, and user support indicators, while profitability was measured by Return on Assets (ROA), listing age by years since the initial public offering, and auditor reputation by Big Four affiliation. The results indicate that profitability has no significant relationship with IFR (B = −0.014, p = 0.431), whereas listing age (B = 0.003, p < 0.001) and auditor reputation (B = 0.019, p = 0.043) have significant positive relationships. The three variables are jointly significant (F = 21.736, p < 0.001), explaining 29.7% of IFR variation (adjusted R² = 0.297). These findings suggest that longer-listed companies and firms audited by Big Four accounting firms demonstrate higher IFR disclosure, while profitability is not significantly associated with IFR. Although limited to profitable energy companies, three predictors, and pooled observations, this study contributes evidence from the first five years of the energy sector as a separate IDX-IC category and provides practical insights for improving corporate financial transparency and supporting investor evaluations.

title: Strategic Management of Industrial Digital Twin Implementation at Oil and Gas, Oil Refining, and Chemical Enterprises
summary: Industrial digital twins are becoming an important instrument of digital transformation in capital-intensive production systems. Their potential value lies in the ability to integrate operational data, engineering models, monitoring, forecasting, scenario analysis, and optimization within a unified framework for supporting managerial decision-making. At the same time, the technical viability of a digital model alone does not guarantee the achievement of sustainable operational or economic outcomes. The purpose of this study is to develop a strategic approach to the implementation of an industrial digital twin that links technological architecture with the business objective, the decision-making system, organizational responsibility, and the validation of the value created. The methodological framework of the study is based on systems analysis, structural decomposition of the digital twin lifecycle, and conceptual synthesis of the managerial conditions required for its implementation. Particular attention is given to enterprises in the oil and gas, oil refining, and chemical industries, which are characterized by high capital intensity, strong technological interdependencies among processes, long asset lifecycles, and high costs associated with erroneous decisions. The maturity of an industrial digital twin is proposed to be assessed according to the extent to which it is integrated into the actual managerial decision-making cycle: from observation and diagnostics to forecasting, scenario analysis, optimization, and decision support. An implementation lifecycle model is developed that encompasses the definition of the business problem, identification of the use case, formulation of expected value, establishment of the governance system, preparation of data and technologies, piloting, organizational integration, operation, outcome assessment, and scaling. The study demonstrates that sustainable implementation requires the coordinated development of technological, informational, and organizational components. Furthermore, scaling involves the replication not only of the software solution itself, but also of the associated system of data, models, processes, responsibilities, and management practices.

title: ESSAYS ON INFORMATION AND DISCLOSURE IN CAPITAL MARKETS: EVIDENCE FROM CLIMATE RISK PRICING AND LABOR INVESTMENT
summary: This dissertation examines how information and disclosure shape outcomes in capital markets, with evidence from two related settings. The first chapter introduces Green Human Capital (GHC), a labor-market-based measure of firms' investment in environmental expertise constructed from employee-level job descriptions, motivated by the question of whether investors price such workforce-level environmental information as a signal of preparedness or of climate risk exposure. I test this by examining how markets react to abnormal GHC around six regulatory events between 2010 and 2022 that progressively increased the likelihood of mandatory climate disclosure. Firms with higher abnormal GHC experience a weakly positive short-window market reaction followed by a sustained negative drift over longer horizons, indicating that investors price GHC predominantly as a signal of climate risk exposure rather than as a value-enhancing capability. This chapter contributes a novel, harder-to-greenwash proxy for environmental orientation to the climate finance literature and shows that workforce-level environmental information is priced directly by outside capital market participants. The second chapter turns to the real effects of disclosure regulation, asking whether an increase in mutual funds' disclosure obligations changes how the firms they invest in change labor investment decisions. I exploit the SEC's 2004 mandate, which raised mutual fund portfolio disclosure frequency from semiannual to quarterly, as a quasi-natural experiment, using a difference-in-differences design that compares firms with high versus low pre-regulation ownership by affected actively managed funds. Treated firms experience a significant deceleration in employment growth following the mandate, accompanied by a shift toward more top-heavy workforce composition and a higher propensity to meet or beat analyst earnings forecasts. This chapter highlights labor investment as an underexamined margin of adjustment to disclosure-driven monitoring pressure. Together, the two chapters show that disclosure regulation's consequences extend beyond the parties directly subject to it, shaping both how markets price firms' human capital investments and how firms allocate labor under heightened monitoring scrutiny.

title: REGULATORY FRAMEWORK FOR THE ACCOUNTING AND AUDITING OF FINANCIAL INSTRUMENTS IN UZBEKISTAN: A CLAUSE-LEVEL COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS WITH IFRS 9 AND ISA 540 (REVISED)
summary: Uzbekistan has transitioned from the voluntary application of International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) to a regulatory framework requiring public interest entities to maintain accounting records and publish audited financial statements in accordance with IFRS, while statutory bookkeeping continues to be governed by national accounting standards (NAS). This study examines the extent to which the regulatory framework in force as of October 2026 supports the accounting and auditing of financial instruments. Thirteen national regulatory acts, including laws, presidential and government resolutions, ministerial orders, and national accounting standards, were systematically mapped at the clause level against IAS 32, IFRS 9, IFRS 7, IFRS 13, and ISA 540 (Revised). The identified differences were classified into five categories: terminological, methodological, taxation-related, auditing-related, and institutional. Of the twelve methodological areas examined, one (foreign-currency revaluation) was found to be aligned, two were partially aligned, and nine were identified as requiring further regulatory and methodological harmonization. In particular, the national chart of accounts and NAS No. 12 do not explicitly incorporate IFRS 9 classification categories, the effective interest method, expected credit loss requirements, financial instrument modification, or hedge accounting. Furthermore, the tax framework does not recognize expected credit losses until the relevant debt is determined to be uncollectible. Although International Standards on Auditing have legal force, further development is required regarding an officially recognized state-language version, national guidance on auditing accounting estimates, and quality-control criteria applicable to such estimates. The study also identifies areas requiring clarification concerning the legal basis for IFRS reporting during the transition between the repeal of the 2020 mandate and the initial obligations established under the 2026 register, as well as the timely recognition of amended IFRS texts. Based on these findings, six groups of recommendations are proposed for consideration in the forthcoming law on accounting and financial reporting and the 2026–2030 audit development concept.

title: The Impact Mechanism and Implementation Path of Green Human Resource Management on the ESG Performance of Enterprises
summary: In the context of the comprehensive green transformation of economic and social development and the significant attention paid by the capital market to ESG values, relying on the internal human resource system to drive the sustainable development of enterprises has become an important research topic. Based on the stakeholder theory, this paper selects green human resource management and the ESG performance of enterprises as the research objects, and uses the mechanism analysis method to explore the intrinsic relationship between the two. The research findings show that green human resource practices can enhance the environmental performance, social performance, and governance performance of enterprises through three paths, and the effect is constrained by industry and property rights characteristics. It also proposes implementation paths such as establishing a hierarchical and classified green training system and improving the green performance assessment and incentive mechanism. This paper expands the research boundary of ESG influencing factors from the perspective of micro internal human resource management and provides references for enterprises to optimize their green human resource systems and implement sustainable development strategies.

title: Reflections on Digital Finance and Artificial Intelligence Driving Corporate Green Innovation Under the Background of Platform Economy
summary: In the process of advancing the dual carbon strategy, the integration of industrial digitalization and green low-carbon development has become a core direction for the transformation of the real economy, with green innovation serving as a key pathway for enterprises to overcome growth constraints and achieve low-carbon upgrades. Currently, domestic enterprises generally face practical challenges in their green transition, including capital shortages, slow technological iteration, and uneven distribution of innovation resources, making traditional development models inadequate to meet the demands of green industries. Leveraging the advantages of platform economies—such as data integration and supply chain connectivity—digital finance and artificial intelligence are gradually emerging as critical tools to support corporate green innovation. This paper examines the application scenarios within the platform economy, focusing on how digital and intelligent technologies empower green innovation, while identifying current issues such as fragmented industry data standards, significant disparities in enterprise transformation, lagging regulatory frameworks, and underdeveloped market mechanisms. Addressing these pain points, the study proposes improvement strategies in areas including data governance, support for small and micro enterprises, regulatory optimization, and the construction of an innovation ecosystem. The findings offer practical guidance for corporate low-carbon transitions and provide theoretical support for the integration of digital and green development, as well as regional low-carbon, high-quality growth.

title: Effects Of Corporate Governance and Financial Leverage of Quoted Deposit Money Banks in Nigeria
summary: This study examines the effect of corporate governance mechanisms on the financial leverage of quoted Deposit Money Banks (DMBs) in Nigeria over the period 2015–2025. Specifically, it investigates the influence of board size, board independence, board composition, gender diversity, and age diversity on leverage levels of listed commercial banks in Nigeria. The study employs a descriptive research design using panel data from 15 quoted DMBs listed on the Nigerian Exchange Group over eleven years (2015–2025). Secondary data were extracted from the annual reports and accounts of the sampled banks. Panel regression models (fixed and random effects) were utilized for data analysis, with the Hausman test applied to determine the most appropriate model specification. Diagnostic tests for heteroskedasticity, serial correlation, and multicollinearity were also conducted. The empirical findings reveal that board size has a significant and positive effect on financial leverage (debt-to-equity ratio) at β = 0.1069 (P-value = 0.0028), consistent with the agency theory perspective that larger boards may facilitate greater debt utilization. Board independence also demonstrates a significant and positive effect on the debt-to-equity ratio at β = 0.0157 (P-value = 0.0000). Furthermore, gender diversity (β = 10.5572; P-value = 0.0000) and age diversity (β = 0.0741; P-value = 0.0132) are found to have significant positive effects on leverage decisions, suggesting that diverse boards are better equipped to assess and manage financial risks. The findings support the Trade-Off Theory, indicating that while high leverage may reduce performance, strong governance mechanisms can mitigate its negative effects. The study provides valuable insights for policymakers, regulators, bank executives, and investors regarding the governance-leverage nexus in the Nigerian banking industry. It extends previous research by incorporating recent data (2015–2025) and multiple governance variables, offering contemporary empirical evidence on the governance-leverage relationship in the Nigerian banking sector during a period of significant regulatory reforms and recapitalization efforts.

title: Business Intelligence Capabilities for Sustainable Supply Chain Performance
summary: Business Intelligence research remains largely technology-focused, leaving the organizational capabilities behind sustainable supply chain outcomes underexplored. This study proposes an integrated framework linking Business Intelligence Capabilities (BIC) to sustainable supply chain performance across economic, environmental, and social dimensions. Drawing on the Dynamic Capabilities Theory and Resource-Based View, the framework treats supply chain visibility, agility, and resilience as key mechanisms through which BIC drives sustainability outcomes, moderated by Data Governance Capability, Top Management Support, and Digital Maturity. With a focus on emerging-economy contexts, still underrepresented in the literature, the study clarifies how BI translates into sustainable performance and offers a foundation for future empirical work, with practical value for managers seeking to leverage BI for sustainable competitive advantage.

title: Pengaruh Penerapan Green Accounting dan Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) Terhadap Kinerja Keuangan: Studi Pada Perusahaan Sektor Perindustrian Yang Terdaftar di Daftar Efek Syariah (DES) Periode 2021–2024
summary: Penelitian ini dilatarbelakangi oleh meningkatnya kesadaran global terhadap keberlanjutan yang mendorong organisasi, termasuk perusahaan berbasis syariah, untuk mempertimbangkan aspek pendapatan, dampak lingkungan, dan dampak sosial. Meskipun demikian, penelitian terdahulu menunjukkan hasil yang inkonsisten mengenai pengaruh Green Accounting dan Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) terhadap kinerja keuangan perusahaan. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh Green Accounting dan CSR secara parsial maupun simultan terhadap kinerja keuangan perusahaan sektor industri yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Syariah (BES) selama periode 2021–2024. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan deskriptif kuantitatif. Biaya lingkungan digunakan sebagai proksi Green Accounting, indeks pengungkapan Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) sebagai proksi CSR, dan Return on Assets (ROA) sebagai proksi kinerja keuangan. Pengambilan sampel dilakukan menggunakan teknik purposive sampling terhadap sembilan perusahaan yang secara konsisten menerbitkan laporan tahunan dan laporan keberlanjutan selama periode 2021–2024, sehingga diperoleh 36 observasi. Data dianalisis menggunakan regresi linier berganda dengan bantuan SPSS versi 29. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa Green Accounting berpengaruh signifikan terhadap kinerja keuangan dengan nilai signifikansi 0,003, sedangkan CSR tidak berpengaruh signifikan dengan nilai signifikansi 0,078. Secara simultan, Green Accounting dan CSR berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap kinerja keuangan perusahaan, dengan nilai Adjusted R² sebesar 37,5%. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa Green Accounting berperan dalam kinerja keuangan perusahaan, sementara pengaruh CSR secara parsial belum terbukti signifikan dalam penelitian ini.

title: Supply Chain Contagion: How Customers’ Abnormal Temperature Exposure Amplifies Suppliers’ Debt Default Risk
summary: Corporate debt defaults are a major source of financial risk and can threaten market stability when they occur on a large scale. Meanwhile, shifts in the global climate and episodes of extreme weather are profoundly altering economies and financial systems. Against this backdrop, examining how temperature-related shocks affect corporate default risk is essential for understanding credit risk transmission under changing environmental conditions. We investigate how customer-side exposure to abnormal temperatures affects suppliers’ debt default risk, using observations for Chinese A-share listed firms over 2008–2023. The findings indicate that suppliers’ debt default risk increases as the annual average temperature in customers’ locations rises further above its long-term historical average. The channel analysis provides evidence consistent with two channels: customers’ abnormal temperature shocks are associated with weaker demand for suppliers’ products and tighter financing conditions, which may help explain the increase in supplier default risk. Heterogeneity tests show that this effect is stronger among suppliers with greater customer dependence or tighter financing constraints, consistent with the demand and financing channels. The effect is also more pronounced for suppliers without green products, whereas stronger ESG performance helps mitigate the adverse impact. Additional analysis links customers’ abnormal temperature exposure to lower subsequent customer concentration among suppliers, suggesting possible adaptation through customer diversification.

title: Atomic Arch: One of the many supply chain attacks.
summary: Abstract: On June 11, 2026, Sonatype researchers disclosed a large-scale supply chain attack against the Arch User Repository (AUR), dubbed Atomic Arch. Attackers systematically claimed ownership of abandoned AUR packages through AUR's standard orphan adoption process, then modified the packages' PKGBUILD files to inject a malicious npm dependency during installation. The dependency delivered a Rust-based infostealer and, when root access was available, an eBPF rootkit. By June 13, the estimated number of compromised packages had grown from 400 to approximately 1,500-1,600. title: The AI SBOM Securing the Supply Chain Beyond the Gateway
summary: Artificial intelligence systems are transforming enterprise infrastructure while expanding the software supply chain attack surface. Traditional Software Bills of Materials (SBOMs) track code dependencies, yet AI introduces opaque components that evade conventional visibility: pre-trained model weights, training datasets, fine-tuning pipelines, and GPU-accelerated infrastructure. The AI-SBOM extends existing SBOM practice to capture the provenance, lineage, and security posture of these components. This article consolidates emerging guidance (the G7 minimum elements for AI SBOMs, CISA's 2025 SBOM minimum elements, and the AI extensions of the SPDX and CycloneDX standards) into an actionable taxonomy for the practicing IT professional, introduces a four-level verifiability grading that turns AI-SBOM trustworthiness into a measurable property, pairs both with a phased implementation roadmap grounded in recent supply chain compromises, and assesses the approach's current limitations. title: INNOVATIONS AND INFLUENCES IN ESG: INSIGHTS FROM AI, BOARD COMPOSITION, AND FAMILY BUSINESS MANAGEMENT
summary: This dissertation consists of three essays that explore different dimensions of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) practices and their implications for corporate reporting and performance. The first essay (Chapter 2) investigates the application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in ESG assurance and its potential to enhance the credibility and reliability of ESG reports. ESG assurance presents greater challenges than traditional financial auditing because of the diversity of ESG topics and information. This essay proposes the use of AI technologies and exogenous data to improve assurance efficiency and effectiveness by enabling auditors to assess large and diverse datasets. It further examines AI applications throughout the ESG assurance process and provides practical implications for auditors, regulators, and stakeholders. The second essay (Chapter 3) examines the relationship between board composition and ESG reporting quality using text mining techniques. Based on 3,449 ESG reports from U.S. public companies, the study finds that board size, gender diversity, and sustainability committees are positively associated with Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) adoption. Gender diversity and sustainability committees are also positively associated with report specificity and relevance. Sustainability committees are associated with a more pessimistic reporting tone, suggesting higher reporting quality. In addition, board size, board independence, and sustainability committees are negatively associated with report readability. These findings provide new evidence on how board characteristics influence qualitative dimensions of ESG reporting. The third essay (Chapter 4) examines family ownership, second-generation management participation, and ESG performance using a sample of Chinese family firms. The findings show that family ownership is negatively associated with ESG performance. However, second-generation participation in management, representing intergenerational succession, improves ESG performance, particularly corporate governance performance. Collectively, these essays contribute to ESG research by integrating emerging technologies, textual analysis, and family business perspectives. The dissertation provides insights for academics studying ESG, governance, and technology; practitioners seeking to improve ESG reporting and performance; and policymakers developing policies that support technological advancement, board diversity, and sustainable family business practices.

title: The Digital Heir: How Next-Generation Successors Experience AI- and FinTech-Enabled Succession in Family Firms
summary: This study examines how next-generation successors experience AI and FinTech-enabled succession in Pakistani family firms. The study is grounded in Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis, with eight semi-structured interviews conducted with second- and third-generation successors across various sectors. The finding reveals three different developmental patterns: evidence-based legitimisation, governance-based integration, and relationally contested recognition. Transitions became more credible because of small digital pilots, measurable results and trusted digital intermediaries, and more successful when digital initiatives were part of formal governance, decision rights were documented, and there was shared accountability. When succession was unclear, digitalisation further exacerbated the intrusion of the incumbent, family dynamics, and the precarious legitimacy of the ruling elites. The study shows that AI and FinTech are not merely operational tools but mechanisms through which authority, trust, continuity, and leadership identity are negotiated. The study contributes to the family business literature by introducing the concept of authority-gated capability development and by showing how socioeconomic wealth can be limiting and facilitating the process of digital transformation in intergenerational succession. title: Factors Affecting Audit Delay
summary: Purpose: This study aims to examine the effects of firm size, profitability, solvency, and audit committee characteristics on audit delay in manufacturing companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX).Methodology: This study employs a quantitative approach using secondary data from audited annual financial reports of manufacturing companies during the 2021–2024 period. The sample was selected using purposive sampling, resulting in 144 companies with 576 firm-year observations. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, classical assumption tests, and multiple linear regression analysis with Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS).Results: The findings show that firm size and profitability have a negative and significant effect on audit delay, indicating that larger and more profitable companies tend to complete audit processes faster. Meanwhile, solvency and audit committee characteristics do not significantly influence audit delay.Conclusion: The study concludes that company resources and financial performance play important roles in improving audit timeliness, while debt structure and audit committee size alone are insufficient to reduce audit delays.Limitation: This study is limited to manufacturing companies listed on the IDX and the explanatory power of the model, suggesting that other factors may contribute to audit delay.Contribution: This study contributes empirical evidence regarding audit delay determinants by highlighting the importance of firm characteristics and governance mechanisms in improving financial reporting timeliness.

title: AISDBM-Agent: An LLM-Enabled Autonomous Decision-Making Prototype System for Intelligent Supply Chain Inventory Optimization
summary: The digital transformation of supply chain operations demands manufacturing systems capable of autonomous decision-making in response to dynamic production fluctuations. However, existing inventory management approaches suffer from limited adaptability to plan variations and delayed response times, primarily due to the absence of tight coupling between inventory control and real-time production demand. To address these challenges, this study proposes AISDBM-Agent, an LLM-enabled autonomous decision-making prototype system for intelligent supply chain inventory optimization. The framework is structured into four functional modules: the perception module receives and translates external multi-source information; the memory module integrates, categorizes, and stores the processed information to mitigate the risks arising from outdated knowledge or contextual inconsistencies; the strategy module utilizes the processed input from the perception module and the knowledge provided by the memory module to perform reasoning and decision-making, automatically generating optimal procurement decisions, employing the Chain of Thought (CoT) method to enhance the transparency and interpretability of these decisions; the execution module interacts with external systems and obtains execution feedback to ensure information timeliness, thereby resolving the issue of delayed response in inventory management. A case study on steel scrap inventory management is conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed framework. The results demonstrate that AISDBM-Agent significantly enhances the system’s ability to respond to fluctuations in demand, enabling the smooth management of stock levels.

title: From tech-driven to principle-driven supply chains: responsible AI governance as a dynamic capability
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in supply-chain forecasting, sourcing, planning, and logistics, yet governance arrangements required to ensure responsible use remain fragmented. This article develops a Responsible AI Governance (RAIG) framework that explains how ethical principles can be translated into operational supply-chain capabilities. Drawing on an integrative synthesis of AI-enabled supply-chain management, responsible AI, dynamic capabilities, relational governance, and socio-technical systems research, the framework connects three principles – transparency and traceability, validity and robustness, and role separation – to four mechanisms: model cards and explainability reports, data and model audits, responsible-sourcing clauses, and human-in-the-loop sales and operations planning reviews. These mechanisms are embedded in procurement, planning, scheduling, and logistics routines and are theorised to support agility, resilience, decarbonisation, and ethically legitimate decision-making. Six propositions specify the framework’s causal logic, while a 90-day implementation playbook translates it into managerial action. The article also develops frugal adaptations for emerging and humanitarian supply chains. Because the field is nascent and access to governance artefacts and data is limited, the study proposes a progressive validation agenda using simulations, vignettes, comparative cases, and micro-pilots. RAIG is positioned as a dynamic capability that turns responsibility from a compliance obligation into an adaptive source of performance.

title: Sea Cucumber Farming and Sasi Tradition: Synergy Between Corporate Social Responsibility and Local Wisdom in Supporting the Conservation of Natural Resources by the Ambel Indigenous Community in Raja Ampat
summary: Sasi represents a form of local wisdom among the people of Raja Ampat for regulating the use of marine resources by managing access to benefits within specific areas or timeframes. However, ensuring the sustainability of its implementation requires overcoming various challenges, thus requiring an approach that supports both conservation and the community’s utilization of natural resources. This study aims to analyze the implementation of the Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) program by PT Pertamina Patra Niaga Refinery Unit (RU) Kasim through the development of sea cucumber aquaculture cages in Waifoi Village, Raja Ampat, and its contribution to the sustainability of community-based natural resource management. The study employed a case study design, with data collected through participatory observation, in-depth interviews, and focus group discussions (FGD). Informants were selected through purposive sampling, taking into account the knowledge and involvement of KTH Waifoi members in the program’s implementation. Data were analyzed descriptively to determine the program’s relevance to the sasi tradition. The results indicate that the sea cucumber aquaculture CSR program aligns with the values of the sasi tradition and supports natural resource management and conservation efforts, particularly regarding sea cucumbers in Waifoi Village

title: Evaluating Automation and Information Management in Sme Operations: Effects on Operational Efficiency and Decision-Making
summary: Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs) increasingly depend on computerized information systems to manage inventory, sales, product information, and other operational activities. Automation can reduce repetitive manual work, while accurate and accessible information can support timely business decision-making. However, the extent to which these capabilities contribute to operational efficiency and decision-making in SME environments requires empirical evaluation. This study evaluated the relationship between automation and operational efficiency and examined the relationship between information quality and accessibility and business decision-making within SME operations, using a computerized inventory/business management system as the practical context. A quantitative survey research design was adopted, and data were collected using a structured questionnaire administered to individuals with experience using or evaluating computerized inventory/business management systems. A total of 106 responses were obtained, of which 103 eligible responses were included in the principal statistical analysis. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Cronbach's alpha, Pearson product-moment correlation, and simple linear regression. The reliability analysis demonstrated acceptable to excellent internal consistency across the principal constructs, with Cronbach's alpha values ranging from 0.741 to 0.915. Automation showed a significant positive relationship with operational efficiency (r = 0.644, p < 0.001) and explained approximately 41.5% of the variance in operational-efficiency scores (R² = 0.415, p < 0.001). Information quality and accessibility demonstrated a stronger positive relationship with decision-making (r = 0.702, p < 0.001) and explained approximately 49.2% of the variance in decision-making (R² = 0.492, p < 0.001). The decision-making construct recorded a mean score of 4.14, indicating a generally positive perception among respondents. However, the image-based product-import feature recorded a comparatively low mean score of 2.46, indicating an area requiring further improvement. The findings indicate that automation is significantly associated with operational efficiency, while information quality and accessibility are significantly associated with business decision-making. The study therefore demonstrates the potential value of computerized information systems in improving SME operations and supporting business decisions, while highlighting the need for continuous improvement of individual automated features, particularly image-based data import. Future research should complement user-perception measures with objective indicators such as task-completion time, data-entry accuracy, and long-term operational performance. Keywords: automation, information management, small and medium-sized enterprises, operational efficiency, decision-making, inventory management, information systems, digital transformation, optical character recognition.

title: TRANSFORMING LIBRARY OPERATIONS THROUGH ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE: THE ROLE OF INTELLIGENT LIBRARY MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS IN THE DIGITAL ERA
summary: AI is now a practical, everyday part of the daily life of 21st-century academic libraries. The integrated library management systems that have traditionally been used for circulation, cataloguing and acquisitions are now supported by chatbot-assisted reference services, automated metadata creation, recommender-based discovery and large language model-enabled scholarly search. This paper reviews the perception of librarians about Intelligent Library Management Systems (ILMS) in the context of its impact on the transformation of library operations in Pakistani universities. The cross sectional survey was given to N = 220 librarians in ten Pakistani universities from January to July 2025. The six latent constructs measured with a five-point Likert scale are: AI Literacy (AIL), Intelligent Library System capabilities (ILS), Operational Efficiency (OPE), Integration Readiness (INT), User Service Quality (USR, mediator) and Transformation Outcomes Perception (TOP, outcome). All constructs had acceptable reliability values (Cronbach α = 0.84 – 0.88; composite reliability values were 0.78 – 0.84; and average variance extracted values were ≥ 0.47). A confirmatory factor model fit the data at conventional thresholds (χ²/df = 1.27; CFI = .951; TLI = .945; RMSEA = .036, 90 % CI [.026, .046]; SRMR = .044). The results of the OLS regression predicting transformation outcomes revealed that AI Literacy (β = +.18, p = .004) and Operational Efficiency (β = +.34, p < .001) each predict outcomes of transformation positively and independently, with Operational Efficiency being the strongest marketing-direct predictor. However, coefficient of the User Service Quality was the second largest (β = +.26, p < .001) and partially mediated the relationship between ILS capabilities and TOP (Sobel z = +3.58, p < .001; indirect effect ≈ 37 % of the total). The direct coefficient was no longer significant when controlling for USR, which was consistent with a "fully-mediated" interpretation of the direct ILS → TOP pathway, rather than "partially-direct". There was no interaction between ILS and Integration-Readiness, as the common assumption that the ILS effect would be multiplicative with Integration-Readiness was rejected (β = +.05, p = .47). Overall model explained 36.1 % of the variance (R² = .361). The pattern indicates that the way library operations are transformed by AI is through two main levers: the operational efficiency provided by the system itself, and the service quality made possible by AI-powered discovery and reference tools, and that upstream investment in AI literacy for librarians is a precondition for the delivery of either of these two levers. title: Artificial Intelligence–Driven Financial Reporting: Transforming Customized Financial Statements, Decision Intelligence, and Assurance Practices
summary: Financial statements are prepared from trial balances that have passed internal-control checks and, for external reporting, have been audited before stakeholders rely on them. Converting this verified ledger into the views needed by investors, creditors, regulators, and management remains largely manual, causing rework, delays, and duplicated reconciliation. This study designs and evaluates an artificial intelligence (AI)-coordinated architecture that generates stakeholder-specific yet reconciled reports from a single governed trial balance. Following a design science approach, the architecture combines centrally configured accounting policies and KPI definitions, lineage metadata, account classification, anomaly detection, sequence forecasting, financial natural language processing (NLP), role-aware customization, and human-in-the-loop explainable AI (XAI). The prototype was evaluated on 15,000 trial balances for 500 entities (12,000 synthetic and 3,000 derived from public SEC filings) against rule-based, robotic process automation (RPA), and commercial generative-AI baselines. It achieved a line-item disclosure fidelity (F1) of 0.965, an AUC of 0.97 for misclassification detection, and a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 4.8% for one- to four-quarter forecasts; in 250 simulated multi-entity scenarios, preparer effort fell from 38.0 to 4.2 person-hours per reporting cycle. Simulated stakeholder and auditor responses illustrate the expected gains in perceived usefulness and trust. Limitations include synthetic and statement-derived data, simulated rather than observed perception measures, and an unevaluated narrative-generation module.

title: Firm Characteristics and Financial Reporting Quality among Listed Non-Financial Companies in Nigeria
summary: The series of corporate failures and reporting irregularities, despite the full adoption of International Financial Reporting Standards, has raised concerns about factors affecting financial reporting quality in Nigeria This study investigated the relationship between firm attributes and financial reporting quality among 85 listed non-financial companies in Nigeria over the period 2016–2025. Financial reporting quality was examined through an income-smoothing index, with auditor type, sustainability disclosure practices and board financial expertise as the principal explanatory variables, with firm size as a control. The reported robust regression results indicated positive and statistically significant associations for auditor type and board financial expertise. Under the interpretation of the index adopted in the manuscript, these findings are consistent with lower income smoothing among firms with the relevant audit and board characteristics. In contrast, sustainability disclosure practices showed a positive but statistically non-significant association, providing insufficient evidence of a relationship within the estimated model. Firm size also demonstrated a positive and significant coefficient. External audit arrangements and board-level financial competence therefore warrant attention. Accordingly, listed companies should apply appropriate professional criteria when selecting external auditors and consider the financial expertise available within their boards. Sustainability disclosure practices may also be integrated with financial reporting processes, although their statistical association with income smoothing was not established in this study. These findings should be interpreted as associations rather than causal effects.

title: Share Option And Performance Of The Agency Model Of Corporate Governance In Managerial Capitalism
summary: This paper examines how share options as executive remuneration affect corporate agents' (managers') performance under the managerial capitalism model in nations where managerial capitalism is prevalent. Recent research shows that the effectiveness of such incentives depends not only on the availability of equity compensation, but also on its design, governance environment, risk characteristics, and link to company performance. Therefore, the share-option performance of the agency model of corporate governance under managerial capitalism is examined in this research. It focuses on how share-option incentives function as a governance instrument, the theoretical justifications for their use, how they affect business performance and management behavior, and the dangers of using excessive or poorly constructed options. To investigate the performance of share options within the agency model of corporate governance under managerial capitalism, we use a qualitative systematic literature-review methodology. Since the goal is to synthesize current theoretical and empirical findings rather than gather primary questionnaire or interview data, the technique is acceptable. Among other things, our results suggest that share options provide a possible agency-alignment mechanism. Additionally, share options might lessen the conflict between management and shareholder interests. Managers are more motivated to engage in activities that raise firm value when a significant portion of executive wealth is based on the company's market worth. The claim that well designed equity incentives may promote management effort and value-enhancing behavior is supported by data from research on productivity, ownership, and risk-taking. Based on our study and data from prior studies, we came to the conclusion that although equity incentives may promote R&D and other potentially value-enhancing activities, option wealth can have a favorable impact on productivity and company value. Therefore, there is a lot of evidence for the fundamental agency thesis that managers who own stock are more inclined to behave in the best interests of shareholders.

title: Corporate Governance and Responsible Lending Practices: Evidence from a Ghanaian Bank
summary: This study examines the influence of corporate governance structures on responsible lending practices within a Ghanaian bank. Despite regulatory reforms, Ghana’s banking sector has experienced persistent challenges with non-performing loans, raising concerns about the effectiveness of governance mechanisms in shaping lending behaviour. Drawing on Agency Theory, Stakeholder Theory, and Signaling Theory, the study adopts a qualitative case study approach using data from document analysis, questionnaires, and semi-structured interviews involving governance, credit, risk, and compliance personnel. The findings indicate that board independence, specialised committees, strong regulatory compliance frameworks, and transparent reporting practices were perceived by participants to enhance lending discipline, risk management effectiveness, and stakeholder confidence. The study contributes to the literature by providing institution-level qualitative evidence from a Ghanaian bank, addressing the limited empirical attention to corporate governance and responsible lending in emerging-market contexts. Its principal contribution is to show how corporate governance mechanisms operate as internal processes that shape responsible lending practices, rather than functioning solely as formal compliance structures. The study further integrates Agency, Stakeholder, and Signaling theories to explain how these mechanisms influence lending discipline, risk management, and stakeholder confidence. The study offers important policy implications for banking supervision and governance reforms in developing economies, emphasizing the need to strengthen board effectiveness and oversight structures to promote responsible lending and financial stability.

title: Blockchain in Supply Chain Transparency, Flexibility, and Supplier Trust in a Lean Perspective
summary: This study examines to analyze the role of blockchain technology in supporting transparency, flexibility, and supplier trust through Lean Supply Chain techniques at PT Siam Cement Group Yogyakarta. The research employs a qualitative approach, utilizing in-depth narrative interviews and direct observation of the implementation of the RMC NET system. Data were gathered from key informants involved in operational activities and system usage, then analyzed through open coding, categorization, cross-informant comparison, and triangulation. The findings indicate that blockchain enhances information visibility and traceability, cross-functional integration, and decision-making rapidity. These factors foster internal transparency, operational flexibility, and the implementation of a Lean Supply Chain by improving process efficiency, productivity, inventory management, delivery performance, processing time, and quality. However, blockchain has not directly shaped supplier trust, which is instead more significantly influenced by performance track records, consistency, communication, and direct interaction.

title: Digital Transformation and Organizational Innovation in Companies Listed on the Tehran Stock Exchange: An Analytical Review and Conceptual Framework
summary: Digital transformation is increasingly treated as a strategic and organizational phenomenon rather than a discrete information-technology project. This analytical review examines how digital transformation can shape organizational innovation and develops a context-sensitive framework for companies listed on the Tehran Stock Exchange (TSE). The review follows a structured narrative approach, synthesizing traceable peer-reviewed research on digital transformation, digital business strategy, dynamic capabilities, digital innovation, organizational innovation, and organizational change. Rather than treating technology investment as a direct cause of innovation, the synthesis identifies a mediated pathway in which digital infrastructure, data and analytics, digital strategy, leadership, human capital, and platform connectivity create value when they are converted into organizational capabilities such as sensing, learning, agility, knowledge integration, cross-functional collaboration, and experimentation. These capabilities can support product and service innovation, process innovation, managerial innovation, and business-model innovation. For listed companies, however, the strength of these relationships is conditioned by governance, disclosure and accountability requirements, data quality and cybersecurity, institutional fit, legacy systems, and organizational inertia. The review therefore proposes that digital transformation should be evaluated as a portfolio of organizational capabilities and governance arrangements rather than by technology adoption alone. For TSE-listed firms, the main implication is that digital investment is most likely to contribute to innovation when technological resources are aligned with strategy, human capabilities, decision rights, and transparent governance. The paper concludes with managerial priorities and a research agenda for empirical testing in the Iranian capital-market context.

title: Firm Attributes and Financial Reporting Quality of Listed Nonfinancial Companies in Nigeria
summary: The series of corporate failures and reporting irregularities despites the full adoption of International Financial Reporting Standards have raised concerns on factors affecting financial reporting quality in Nigeria. Consequently, the main objective of this study was to investigate the effect of firm attributes on financial reporting quality of listed nonfinancial companies in Nigeria. Specifically, this study examined how auditor type, sustainability disclosure practices, board financial expertise, affect income smoothing. The research design adopted in this study was ex post facto, secondary data were used and the population of the study was 100 listed nonfinancial companies out of which 85 companies were purposively selected as the sample size. The technique of data analysis employed was panel regression analysis and the statistical package used was STATA 17. The findings of the study revealed that auditor type has a positive and statistically significant effect (coeff. = 0.387, p = 0.007); sustainability disclosure practices (SUDP) has a positive but statistically nonsignificant effect(coeff. = 0.525, p = 0.491); and board financial expertise has a positive and statistically significant effect (coeff. = 1.597, p = 0.038) on income smoothing of listed non-financial firms in Nigeria. It was thus concluded that firm attributesare fundamental in reducing income smoothing and enhancing the financial reporting quality among listed non-financial companies in Nigeria. It was therefore recommended amongst others that the management of these firms should strengthen the independence of audit committees to enhance their oversight role and reduce opportunities for earnings manipulation.

title: Government Policy Instruments and Sustainable Supply Chain Management Adoption in Resource-Intensive and High-Impact Industries: A Critical Integrative Review
summary: Government policy is often treated as an external driver of sustainable supply chain management (SSCM), yet policy exposure need not produce durable supplier-facing change. This critical integrative review develops a functional taxonomy of capability-building, coercive enforcement, market-shaping, information-forcing, and orchestration instruments. A retrospective source-critical audit retained 100 full-text publications from an original 103-publication inventory: 96 substantive sources and four methodological anchors. The synthesis distinguishes policy exposure, adoption quality, and downstream sustainability effectiveness. It proposes capability support, enforcement credibility, and observability and verification as potentially complementary conditions, not empirically established necessities. Source-level contrasts show that support can have opposite associations across supplier practices, environmental and financial outcomes can diverge, and improved disclosure need not establish remediation. Resource intensity and high impact are defined at the process and supply-chain level, with six boundary dimensions specifying transfer. Operational proxies and a proposition-specific testing roadmap are provided. The audit supplies design-sensitive limitations and source-page anchors; missing historical search records, single-reviewer interpretation, and heterogeneous measures constrain coverage and causal inference. The contribution is a mechanism-based framework for empirical testing, not a causal ranking of policy instruments.

title: Essential Characteristics and Results of the Digital China Strategy for Digital Transformation of the Infrastructure of the Chinese Economy
summary: With the advent of the digital economy era, the role of digital infrastructure is becoming increasingly significant. It accelerates the digital transformation of traditional industries, promotes the development of new industries, new formats and new business models of the economy. Therefore, advanced countries are investing heavily in the digitalization of the economic infrastructure, receiving enormous economic returns. The article presents the results of the analysis of the digital transformation of the economic infrastructure of China (PRC). The object of the study is the economic infrastructure of China (PRC). The subject of the study is the directions, forms and mechanisms of digital transformation of the economic infrastructure of China. The objective of the study is to determine the level and specifics of the digital transformation of the economic infrastructure of China (PRC). To achieve this objective, the following tasks were set and solved: theoretical and practical aspects of the digital transformation of the economic infrastructure of China were studied, systematized and generalized; The digital transformation of China's economic infrastructure was found to be in line with the directions and objectives outlined in the government programs and plans of the PRC Government and the Communist Party of China, including the "Digital China" and "Digital Silk Road" strategies, which play a key role in the digital transformation of China's economic infrastructure. Recommendations were formulated for adapting China's positive experience to the digital transformation of Russia's economic infrastructure. The study utilized general scientific research methods: analysis and synthesis. Russian, Chinese, and other international sources served as the theoretical and methodological basis for the study. The study's scientific novelty lies in the comprehensive nature of the analysis and the presentation of the essence of all programs and plans of the PRC Government and the CPC aimed at the digital transformation of China's economic infrastructure. The study achieved its stated goal: it identified the specifics of the digital transformation of China's economic infrastructure, which consists of implementing digitalization based on an active government policy and significant government investment in all areas of the digital transformation of China's economic infrastructure. The results of the study led to the conclusion that China has competitive advantages in the digital transformation of economic infrastructure and, due to these advantages, has every reason to become a prototype for the digital transformation of the Russian economic infrastructure.
